The '''2019 Canadian federal election''' was held on October 21, 2019. [[Member of Parliament (Canada)|Members]] of the [[House of Commons of Canada|House of Commons]] were elected to the [[43rd Canadian Parliament]]. In keeping with the [[Fixed election dates in Canada#Federal|maximum four-year term]] under a [[Canada Elections Act#Notable provisions|2007 amendment to the ''Canada Elections Act'']], the [[writs of election]] for the 2019 election were issued by [[Governor General of Canada|Governor General]] [[Julie Payette]] on September 11, 2019.

With 33.12% of the vote for the [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]], led by incumbent [[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]], the 2019 election set, at the time, a record for the lowest vote share for a party that would go on to form a single-party [[Federal minority governments in Canada|minority government]] (this record would later be beaten in the subsequent [[2021 Canadian federal election|2021 federal election]]).<ref name="np">{{Cite news |date=October 22, 2019 |title=All-time low share of popular vote is enough for Liberals to win power |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/election-2019/canadian-federal-election-2019-liberals-justin-trudeau-win |access-date=October 22, 2019 |website=National Post |last1=Brean |first1=Joseph |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706201852/https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/election-2019/canadian-federal-election-2019-liberals-justin-trudeau-win |url-status=live }}</ref> The Liberals lost the popular vote to the [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative Party]] by one per cent,<ref name="Zimonjic-2019a">{{Cite web |last=Zimonjic |first=Peter |date=October 22, 2019 |title=Liberals take losses but win enough in Quebec and Ontario to form minority government |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/federal-election-results-2019-cbc-leaders-1.5329485 |access-date=October 21, 2019 |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |archive-date=October 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191022165202/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/federal-election-results-2019-cbc-leaders-1.5329485 |url-status=live }}</ref> marking only the second time in Canadian history that a governing party formed a government while receiving less than 35 per cent of the national popular vote, the first time being the inaugural [[1867 Canadian federal election]] after [[Canadian Confederation|Confederation]]. It was also the first time since [[1979 Canadian federal election|1979]] that the party with the most votes overall did not win the most seats, and the first election since [[1926 Canadian federal election|1926]] in which the Liberals won the most seats without receiving the most votes. 

The Conservatives, led by [[Andrew Scheer]], won 121 seats and remained the [[Official Opposition (Canada)|Official Opposition]]. The [[Bloc Québécois]], led by [[Yves-François Blanchet]], won 32 seats to regain [[official party status]] and became the third party for the first time since [[2008 Canadian federal election|2008]]. The [[New Democratic Party]], led by [[Jagmeet Singh]], won 24 seats, its worst result since [[2004 Canadian federal election|2004]]. The [[Green Party of Canada|Green Party]], led by [[Elizabeth May]], saw its best election results with three seats and for the first time received over one million votes. The Greens also elected their first MP outside of British Columbia, [[Jenica Atwin]] in [[Fredericton (federal electoral district)|Fredericton]], New Brunswick.<ref name="Zimonjic-2019a"/> [[Independent politician|Independent]] MP [[Jody Wilson-Raybould]] won her seat and was the first independent to win a seat in over a decade. In their first election, the [[People's Party of Canada|People's Party]] failed to win any seats, as leader [[Maxime Bernier]] lost his own seat in [[Beauce (electoral district)|Beauce]], a seat he won as a Conservative in the previous four elections before forming his own party following his [[2017 Conservative Party of Canada leadership election|unsuccessful bid for the Conservative Party's leadership]].

==Background==
The [[2015 Canadian federal election|2015 federal election]] resulted in a [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal]] [[majority government]] headed by [[Justin Trudeau]]. The [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservatives]] became the Official Opposition (with [[Stephen Harper]] announcing his resignation as party leader) and the [[New Democratic Party|New Democrats]] (NDP) became the third party. While members of the [[Bloc Québécois]] and the [[Green Party of Canada|Greens]] were elected to the House, both failed to achieve the required number of MPs—twelve—for official party status. Bloc leader [[Gilles Duceppe]] announced his resignation shortly after the election, and was succeeded by [[Parti Québécois]] MNA [[Martine Ouellet]].<ref name="ouelett">{{Cite web |last=Riga |first=Andy |date=March 14, 2017 |title=Bloc Québécois' new leader: Who is Martine Ouellet? |url=https://montrealgazette.com/news/local-news/bloc-quebecois-leadership-who-is-martine-ouellet |access-date=March 14, 2017 |website=The Gazette |location=Montreal |archive-date=August 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813185103/https://montrealgazette.com/news/local-news/bloc-quebecois-leadership-who-is-martine-ouellet |url-status=live }}</ref> After losing a [[leadership review]], Ouellet announced she would step down as Bloc leader on June 11, 2018,<ref name=ouellet_resignation/> and was succeeded by [[Yves-François Blanchet]] on January 17, 2019.<ref name="BlanchetWins">{{Cite news |date=January 17, 2019 |title=Yves-François Blanchet becomes Bloc Québécois leader |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/yves-fran-ois-blanchet-new-bloc-leader-1.4981556 |access-date=January 17, 2019 |archive-date=November 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191114025331/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/yves-fran-ois-blanchet-new-bloc-leader-1.4981556 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Tom Mulcair]] was rejected as NDP party leader; he gained only 48% of the vote at the NDP's April 2016 [[leadership review]]. The party held a [[2017 New Democratic Party leadership election|leadership election]] on October 1, 2017, electing Ontario MPP and the former Deputy Leader of the [[Ontario New Democratic Party]] [[Jagmeet Singh]] as Mulcair's successor.<ref name="2016NDPConvention-CP" /><ref name="Kirkup">{{Cite web |last=Kirkup |first=Kristy |date=October 1, 2017 |title=Jagmeet Singh named leader of the federal NDP |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/ndp-chooses-young-charismatic-jagmeet-singh-as-new-leader/ |access-date=October 1, 2017 |website=CTV News |archive-date=October 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171002070453/http://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/jagmeet-singh-named-leader-of-the-federal-ndp-1.3614296 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Bill C-44===
Bill C-44 was passed in 2017 and assigned responsibility to the [[Parliamentary Budget Officer|Parliamentary Budget Office]] to calculate the cost of party platforms for elections; the review was available in the 2019 election. The Parliamentary Budget Office had a $500,000 budget for costing party platforms for this election, but announced it would only review a party platform at the request of the authoring party. It also conducted confidential assessments of independent and party platform proposals preceding the election campaign. The service was also available to members of parliament representing a party without official party status in the House of Commons, like [[Elizabeth May]]'s Green Party.<ref name="Beeby">{{Cite news |last=Beeby |first=Dean |date=April 18, 2019 |title=PBO launches new service to cost out party platforms, despite the political risks |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/parliamentary-budget-officer-giroux-page-election-costing-parties-platform-netherlands-1.5100218 |access-date=April 18, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202043/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/parliamentary-budget-officer-giroux-page-election-costing-parties-platform-netherlands-1.5100218 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Electoral reform===
{{main|Canadian House of Commons Special Committee on Electoral Reform}}
In the lead-up to the 2015 federal election, Trudeau committed to replacing [[first-past-the-post voting]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Geddes |first=John |date=June 27, 2015 |title=Can Justin Trudeau fix the vote with electoral reform? |url=http://www.macleans.ca/politics/ottawa/trudeau-fixing-the-vote/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706201907/https://www.macleans.ca/politics/ottawa/trudeau-fixing-the-vote/ |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |access-date=January 9, 2016 |website=Maclean's}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=January 6, 2016 |title=Justin Trudeau unveils Liberal platform |url=http://www.cbc.ca/player/play/2669555761 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160205054237/http://www.cbc.ca/player/play/2669555761 |archive-date=February 5, 2016 |access-date=January 9, 2016 |work=CBC Player}}</ref> but the [[First-past-the-post voting|first-past-the-post]] electoral system was ultimately retained.

Following the Liberal victory, the [[Canadian House of Commons Special Committee on Electoral Reform|Special Committee on Electoral Reform]] was formed, and in December 2016 recommended a [[Proportional representation|proportional electoral system]] be introduced following a national referendum.<ref name="ERRErecommend">{{Cite news |last=Wherry |first=Aaron |date=December 1, 2016 |title=Electoral reform committee recommends referendum on proportional representation, but Liberals disagree |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC News]] |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/wherry-electoral-reform-committee-1.3866879 |access-date=July 28, 2021 |archive-date=April 12, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180412133850/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/wherry-electoral-reform-committee-1.3866879 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bryden |first=Joan |date=December 1, 2016 |title=Liberal MPs urge Prime Minister to break promise of new voting system by next election |work=[[Ottawa Citizen]] |url=https://ottawacitizen.com/news/politics/all-party-committee-recommends-proportional-voting-system-referendum |access-date=July 28, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202043/https://ottawacitizen.com/news/politics/all-party-committee-recommends-proportional-voting-system-referendum |url-status=live }}</ref> The report was criticized by [[Minister of Democratic Institutions]] [[Maryam Monsef]] for not recommending a specific electoral system, though the committee argued that it had fulfilled its mandate.<ref name="ERRErecommend" /> In February 2017, Trudeau issued a mandate to newly-appointed Minister of Democratic Institutions [[Karina Gould]] which dropped the issue, on the grounds that "A clear preference for a new electoral system, let alone a consensus, has not emerged."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wherry |first=Aaron |date=February 1, 2017 |title=Opposition accuses Trudeau of 'betrayal' as Liberals abandon promise of electoral reform |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-electoral-reform-mandate-1.3961736 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706201901/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-electoral-reform-mandate-1.3961736 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |access-date=February 1, 2017 |publisher=[[CBC News]]}}</ref>

===Assessment of Trudeau's government===
In July 2019, an independent academically edited study, ''Assessing Justin Trudeau's Liberal Government: 353 Promises and a Mandate for Change'', was published by Les Presses de l'[[Université Laval]], finding that Justin Trudeau's government kept 92 per cent of pledges, when complete and partial pledges were added together, while the Harper government kept 85 per cent of complete and partial pledges. When only completed, realized pledges were calculated, Harper's government, in their last year, kept 77 per cent of promises while the Liberal government kept 53.5 per cent. The book notes that Harper's pledges tended towards transactional pledges which target sub-populations while Trudeau's government's promises were transformative—ambitious pledges the Liberals took while they were the third-place party. Trudeau's government, according to the researchers, and the "last Harper government had the highest rates of follow-through on their campaign promises of any Canadian government over the last 35 years."<ref>{{Cite book |last=Lisa |first=François |url=https://www.pulaval.com/produit/assessing-justin-trudeau-s-liberal-government |title=Assessing Justin Trudeau's Liberal Government. 353 promises and a mandate for change |date=July 2019 |publisher=Presses de l'Université Laval |isbn=978-2-7637-4443-8 |edition=first |location=Quebec City |pages=262 |access-date=October 13, 2019 |archive-date=October 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013172816/https://www.pulaval.com/produit/assessing-justin-trudeau-s-liberal-government |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Blatchford |first=Andy |date=August 25, 2019 |title=New book examines Trudeau government's record of living up to pledges |work=The Globe and Mail |agency=The Canadian Press |location=Ottawa |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-new-book-examines-trudeau-governments-record-of-living-up-to-pledges/ |access-date=October 13, 2019 |archive-date=September 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190907213838/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-new-book-examines-trudeau-governments-record-of-living-up-to-pledges/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Election spending===
According to Elections Canada rules, third parties are allowed to spend $1,023,400 in the pre-election period between June 30 and the start of the election campaign. They can spend an additional $511,700 during the election campaign.<ref name="Carman-2019">{{Cite news |last=Carman |first=Tara |date=October 18, 2019 |title=Unions top funders of third party election ads, financial records show |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/elections/unions-third-party-ads-finance-1.5325330 |access-date=October 18, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210317/https://www.cbc.ca/news/elections/unions-third-party-ads-finance-1.5325330 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Third Party Expenses Limits |url=https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&document=index&dir=thi/limits&lang=e |access-date=October 28, 2019 |website=Elections Canada |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202047/https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&document=index&dir=thi%2Flimits&lang=e |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Reimbursements for political parties and candidates ====
Political parties receive a reimbursement for 50 per cent of their election expenses during the writ period. Similarly, electoral district associations receive a reimbursement of 60 per cent of their election expenses during the writ period. Both reimbursements are publicly funded.<ref name="elections.ca2">{{Cite web |title=Elections Canada Online – The Electoral System of Canada |url=http://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=res&dir=ces&document=part6&lang=e |access-date=August 3, 2015 |website=Elections Canada |archive-date=August 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150820005709/http://elections.ca/content.aspx?section=res&dir=ces&document=part6&lang=e |url-status=live }}</ref>{{efn|While the source is from 2015, this still applied to 2019}}

==== Registered third parties ====
A person or group must register as a [[Registered third parties (Canada)|third party]] immediately after incurring expenses totaling $500 or more on regulated activities that take place during the pre-election period or election period. The regulated activities are partisan activities (that promote parties or candidates), election surveys, partisan advertising and election advertising. Furthermore, to be a third party you must be :

* an individual who is a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident or lives in Canada
* a corporation that carries on business in Canada, or
* a group, as long as a person responsible for the group is a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident or lives in Canada.

One cannot spend money or use their resources to influence Canadian elections if they are a foreign third party.

There are also strict limits on expenses related to regulated activities, and specific limits that can be incurred to promote or oppose the election of one or more candidates in a particular electoral district. Registered third parties are subject to an election advertising expenses limit of $1,023,400 in the pre-election period, of which $10,234 can be spent in a given electoral district and $511,700 during the election period. Of that amount, no more than $4,386 can be spent to promote or oppose the election of one or more candidates in a particular electoral district.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Third Party Roadmap |url=https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&document=index&dir=thi/roadmap&lang=e |access-date=November 3, 2019 |website=Elections Canada |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706201913/https://www.elections.ca/error.aspx?aspxerrorpath=%2Fcontent.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=New Requirements for Third Parties: Corporations, Unions, Groups and Individuals |url=https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&dir=thi&document=backgrounder&lang=e#q3 |access-date=November 3, 2019 |website=Elections Canada |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706201855/https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&dir=thi&document=backgrounder&lang=e#q3 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Political Financing Handbook for Third Parties, Financial Agents and Auditors (EC 20227) – August 2019 |url=https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&dir=thi/ec20227&document=p4&lang=e |access-date=November 3, 2019 |website=Elections Canada |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706201915/https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=pol&dir=thi%2Fec20227&document=p4&lang=e |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2015===
*October 19, 2015: The [[Liberal Party of Canada]] wins a [[majority government]] in the [[2015 Canadian federal election|42nd Canadian federal election]]. Outgoing Prime Minister [[Stephen Harper]] announces his intention to resign as leader of the [[Conservative Party of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dehaas |first=Josh |date=October 19, 2015 |title=Stephen Harper resigns as Conservative leader |work=[[CTV News]] |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/stephen-harper-resigns-as-conservative-leader/ |access-date=October 19, 2015 |archive-date=October 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151020035634/http://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/stephen-harper-resigns-as-conservative-leader-1.2617950 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*October 22, 2015: [[Gilles Duceppe]] resigns as leader of the [[Bloc Québécois]] and is replaced on an interim-basis by [[Rivière-du-Nord (electoral district)|Rivière-du-Nord]] MP [[Rhéal Fortin]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Perreaux |first=Les |date=October 22, 2015 |title=Bloc leader Duceppe, former PQ interim leader both resign |work=The Globe and Mail |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/former-pq-interim-leader-stephane-bedard-leaving-politics/article26925216/ |access-date=November 5, 2015 |archive-date=April 4, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170404163311/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/former-pq-interim-leader-stephane-bedard-leaving-politics/article26925216/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
*November 4, 2015: [[Justin Trudeau]] is sworn in as the [[List of prime ministers of Canada|23rd]] [[Prime Minister of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=O'Malley |first=Kady |date=October 28, 2015 |title=Lifting the curtain on Harper's covert exit strategy |work=Ottawa Citizen |url=https://ottawacitizen.com/news/politics/kady-lifting-the-curtain-on-harpers-covert-exit-strategy |access-date=October 29, 2015 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202828/https://ottawacitizen.com/news/politics/kady-lifting-the-curtain-on-harpers-covert-exit-strategy |url-status=live }}</ref>
*November 5, 2015: [[Sturgeon River—Parkland]] MP and former cabinet minister [[Rona Ambrose]] is elected interim [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative]] leader.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 5, 2015 |title=Rona Ambrose named interim leader of the Conservative Party of Canada |work=National Post |agency=The Canadian Press |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/rona-ambrose-named-interim-leader-of-the-conservative-party-of-canada |access-date=November 5, 2015 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202858/https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/rona-ambrose-named-interim-leader-of-the-conservative-party-of-canada |url-status=live }}</ref>
*December 3, 2015: The [[42nd Canadian Parliament|42nd Parliament]] is convened.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mehler Paperny |first=Anna |date=November 4, 2015 |title=Canada's parliament will reconvene in December |work=Global News |url=http://globalnews.ca/news/2319232/canadas-parliament-will-reconvene-in-december/ |access-date=November 5, 2015 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202833/https://globalnews.ca/news/2319232/canadas-parliament-will-reconvene-in-december/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2016===
*March 23, 2016: [[Jim Hillyer (politician)|Jim Hillyer]], Conservative MP for [[Medicine Hat—Cardston—Warner]] dies of a heart attack.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Franklin |first=Michael |date=March 23, 2016 |title=Southern Alberta MP Jim Hillyer found dead in his office |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/calgary/article/southern-alberta-mp-jim-hillyer-found-dead-in-his-office/ |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=[[CTV News]] |location=Calgary |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202829/https://calgary.ctvnews.ca/southern-alberta-mp-jim-hillyer-found-dead-in-his-office-1.2829271 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*April 10, 2016: 52% of delegates at the 2016 [[New Democratic Party|NDP]] convention voted in support of a [[leadership review]] motion to hold a [[2017 New Democratic Party leadership election|leadership election]] within 24 months.<ref name="2016NDPConvention-CP">{{Cite news |last=Kirkup |first=Kristy |date=April 10, 2016 |title=NDP rejects Mulcair as leader, votes in support of holding leadership race |work=[[Ottawa Citizen]] |agency=[[The Canadian Press]] |url=https://ottawacitizen.com/news/politics/ndp-votes-for-leadership-review-mulcair-likely-out-as-leader |access-date=April 10, 2016 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202836/https://ottawacitizen.com/news/politics/ndp-votes-for-leadership-review-mulcair-likely-out-as-leader |url-status=live }}</ref> Party leader [[Tom Mulcair]] announces he will stay on as leader until his replacement is chosen.<ref name="2016NDPConventionCBC">{{Cite news |last=Wherry |first=Aaron |date=April 10, 2016 |title=NDP votes in favour of holding new leadership race |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/mulcair-ndp-leadership-1.3529013 |access-date=April 10, 2016 |archive-date=April 10, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160410160925/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/mulcair-ndp-leadership-1.3529013 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*August 15, 2016: [[Mauril Bélanger|Mauril Belanger]], Liberal MP for [[Ottawa—Vanier (federal electoral district)|Ottawa—Vanier]] dies of [[Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis|ALS]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 16, 2016 |title=MP Mauril Bélanger dies after battle with ALS |work=The Globe and Mail |agency=The Canadian Press |location=Ottawa |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/mp-mauril-belanger-passes-away-after-battle-with-als/article31440561/ |access-date=March 30, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202838/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/politics/mp-mauril-belanger-passes-away-after-battle-with-als/article31440561/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
*August 26, 2016: Former Prime Minister [[Stephen Harper]], Conservative MP for [[Calgary Heritage]] resigns his seat in the House of Commons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Right Honourable Stephen Harper – Overview – House of Commons of Canada |url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/1733?name=Harper,-Stephen-(Right-Hon) |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803021109/https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/1733?name=Harper%2C-Stephen-(Right-Hon) |archive-date=August 3, 2019 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=ourcommons.ca}}</ref>
*September 9, 2016: [[Strength in Democracy]], a party which had three incumbent MPs among its 17 candidates in the last election is deregistered by Elections Canada for failure to file papers maintaining its party status.<ref name="SiD deregistration">{{Cite news |last=Grenier |first=Éric |date=September 9, 2016 |title=Start-up party Strength in Democracy deregistered by Elections Canada |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/grenier-strength-in-democracy-1.3755101 |access-date=October 17, 2016 |archive-date=September 11, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911032340/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/grenier-strength-in-democracy-1.3755101 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*September 23, 2016: [[Jason Kenney]], Conservative MP for [[Calgary Midnapore]] resigns his seat to seek the leadership of the [[Progressive Conservative Association of Alberta]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cochrane |first=David |date=July 7, 2016 |title=Taxpayers group miffed Kenney will collect MP perks this summer |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/jason-kenney-canadian-taxpayers-federation-alberta-1.3668514 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202905/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/jason-kenney-canadian-taxpayers-federation-alberta-1.3668514 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2017===
*February 1, 2017: [[John McCallum]], Liberal MP for [[Markham—Thornhill (federal electoral district)|Markham—Thornhill]] resigns his seat to become [[List of ambassadors of Canada to China|Ambassador to China]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Honourable John McCallum – Overview – House of Commons of Canada |url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/1817?name=McCallum,-John-(Hon) |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813185656/https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/1817?name=McCallum,-John-(Hon) |archive-date=August 13, 2019 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=ourcommons.ca}}</ref>
*February 6, 2017: [[Stéphane Dion]], Liberal MP for [[Saint-Laurent (federal electoral district)|Saint-Laurent]] resigns his seat to become [[List of ambassadors of Canada to Germany|Ambassador to Germany]] and Special Envoy of Canada to the [[European Union]] and Europe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Honourable Stéphane Dion – Overview – House of Commons of Canada |url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/460?name=Dion,-Stephane-(Hon) |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813185705/https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/460?name=Dion,-Stephane-(Hon) |archive-date=August 13, 2019 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=ourcommons.ca}}</ref>
*March 18, 2017: [[Martine Ouellet]] [[2017 Bloc Québécois leadership election|is acclaimed]] as leader of the [[Bloc Québécois]].<ref name="ouelett" />
*May 27, 2017: [[Andrew Scheer]] is [[2017 Conservative Party of Canada leadership election|elected]] leader of the [[Conservative Party of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 27, 2017 |title=Andrew Scheer is the new leader of the Conservative Party of Canada |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/andrew-scheer-is-the-new-leader-of-the-conservative-party-of-canada |access-date=May 27, 2017 |website=National Post |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202819/https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/andrew-scheer-is-the-new-leader-of-the-conservative-party-of-canada?r |url-status=live }}</ref>
*July 4, 2017: [[Rona Ambrose]], Conservative MP for [[Sturgeon River—Parkland]] resigns her seat in the House of Commons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Honourable Rona Ambrose – Overview – House of Commons of Canada |url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/25447?name=Ambrose,-Rona-(Hon) |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803021159/https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/25447?name=Ambrose%2C-Rona-(Hon) |archive-date=August 3, 2019 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=ourcommons.ca}}</ref>
*August 31, 2017: [[Calgary Skyview]] MP [[Darshan Kang]] resigns from the Liberal caucus amid sexual harassment allegations.<ref name="KangResign2017" />
*September 14, 2017: [[Arnold Chan]], Liberal MP for [[Scarborough—Agincourt (federal electoral district)|Scarborough—Agincourt]] dies of cancer.<ref name="Chan2017" /><ref name="ChanCBC">{{Cite web |last=Wherry |first=Aaron |date=September 14, 2017 |title=Toronto-area Liberal MP Arnold Chan dies at 50 |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/arnold-chan-death-1.4289409 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202854/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/arnold-chan-death-1.4289409 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*October 1, 2017: [[Jagmeet Singh]] is [[2017 New Democratic Party leadership election|elected]] leader of the [[New Democratic Party]].<ref name="date">{{Cite news |last=Milewski |first=Terry |date=May 15, 2016 |title=NDP sets leadership convention for fall of 2017 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/ndp-leadership-convention-date-1.3583438 |access-date=July 5, 2017 |archive-date=June 10, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610230347/http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/ndp-leadership-convention-date-1.3583438 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Kirkup" />
*December 1, 2017: [[Denis Lemieux]], Liberal MP for [[Chicoutimi—Le Fjord]] resigns his seat in the House of Commons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denis Lemieux – Overview – House of Commons of Canada |url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/88446?name=Lemieux,-Denis |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803021250/https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/88446?name=Lemieux%2C-Denis |archive-date=August 3, 2019 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=ourcommons.ca}}</ref>

===2018===
*February 28, 2018: Citing conflict with party leader [[Martine Ouellet]], seven [[Bloc Québécois]] MPs resign from the party caucus,<ref name="7 out of 10 bloc" /> establishing the {{lang|fr|[[Groupe parlementaire québécois]]}} for parliamentary purposes, while remaining independent of any electoral political party.<ref name="Ballingall" /> Only [[Xavier Barsalou-Duval]] ([[Pierre-Boucher—Les Patriotes—Verchères]]), [[Mario Beaulieu (politician)|Mario Beaulieu]] ([[La Pointe-de-l'Île]]), and [[Marilène Gill]] ([[Manicouagan (electoral district)|Manicouagan]]) remain in the Bloc Québécois caucus.
*May 2, 2018: [[Gord Brown]], Conservative MP for [[Leeds—Grenville—Thousand Islands and Rideau Lakes (federal electoral district)|Leeds—Grenville—Thousand Islands and Rideau Lakes]] dies of a heart attack.<ref name="GordBrownCBC" />
*May 9, 2018: Members of the ''Groupe parlementaire québécois'' announce they will be forming a new political party, [[Québec debout]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Marotta |first=Stefanie |date=May 9, 2018 |title=Bloc rebels announce new party name and abandon the separatist program |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/new-party-quebec-debout-1.4655698 |access-date=May 11, 2018 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202823/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/new-party-quebec-debout-1.4655698 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*June 4, 2018: After losing a [[leadership review]], [[Martine Ouellet]] announces she will step down as leader of the [[Bloc Québécois]] effective June 11, 2018.<ref name="ouellet_resignation">{{Cite news |last=Tunney |first=Catharine |date=June 4, 2018 |title=Embattled Bloc Québécois leader Martine Ouellet resigns |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/martine-ouellet-steps-down-1.4690336 |access-date=June 4, 2018 |archive-date=November 9, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109024527/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/martine-ouellet-steps-down-1.4690336 |url-status=live }}</ref> 
*June 6, 2018: [[Michel Boudrias]] and [[Simon Marcil]], [[Québec debout]] MPs for [[Terrebonne (federal electoral district)|Terrebonne]] and [[Mirabel (federal electoral district)|Mirabel]], respectively, announce they will return to the [[Bloc Québécois]] caucus as a result of [[Martine Ouellet]]'s resignation as party leader.<ref name=Boudrias_Marcil/> Citing the Bloc's vote the previous weekend to focus exclusively on [[Quebec sovereignty movement|Quebec sovereignty]], Québec debout spokesman [[Rhéal Fortin]] announces that he and the party's other four MPs will not rejoin the Bloc Québécois.<ref name=Boudrias_Marcil/>
*August 3, 2018: [[Tom Mulcair]], NDP MP for [[Outremont (electoral district)|Outremont]] resigns his seat in the House of Commons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Honourable Thomas J. Mulcair – Overview – House of Commons of Canada |url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/26684?name=Mulcair,-Thomas-(Hon) |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803021406/https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/26684?name=Mulcair%2C-Thomas-(Hon) |archive-date=August 3, 2019 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=ourcommons.ca}}</ref>
*August 23, 2018: [[Beauce (electoral district)|Beauce]] MP [[Maxime Bernier]] resigns from the [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative]] caucus in disagreement with the leadership of [[Andrew Scheer]]. Bernier announces his intention to form a new federal party.<ref name="BernierCBC2018" />
*September 14, 2018: 
**Three weeks after leaving the [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative]] caucus, [[Beauce (electoral district)|Beauce]] MP [[Maxime Bernier]] formally launches the [[People's Party of Canada]], becoming its first MP.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 14, 2018 |title=Bernier faces a challenge keeping racists out of his new party, says Stockwell Day |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/bernier-peoples-party-canada-1.4823647 |access-date=September 14, 2018 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202906/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/bernier-peoples-party-canada-1.4823647 |url-status=live }}</ref>
**[[Kennedy Stewart (Canadian politician)|Kennedy Stewart]], [[New Democratic Party|NDP]] MP for [[Burnaby South]], resigns to run for [[mayor of Vancouver]], triggering a by-election in his riding.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1025145722289569792 |user=kennedystewart |title=As promised, I've submitted my resignation letter. I'll continue my MP duties until Sept 14 when I officially file as a #Vancouver mayoral candidate. It's been a great honour to serve my constituents for the last seven years. #ndp #vanpoli |date=August 2, 2018 |first=Kennedy |last=Stewart}}</ref>
*September 17, 2018:
** All five [[Québec debout]] MPs – [[Rhéal Fortin]] ([[Rivière-du-Nord (electoral district)|Rivière-du-Nord]]), [[Monique Pauzé]] ([[Repentigny (federal electoral district)|Repentigny]]), [[Louis Plamondon]] ([[Bécancour—Nicolet—Saurel]]), [[Gabriel Ste-Marie]] ([[Joliette (federal electoral district)|Joliette]]), and [[Luc Thériault]] ([[Montcalm (federal electoral district)|Montcalm]]) – announce they will rejoin the [[Bloc Québécois]],<ref name=deboutBloc/> officially dissolving Quebec debout.
** [[Leona Alleslev]], [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal]] MP for [[Aurora—Oak Ridges—Richmond Hill (federal electoral district)|Aurora—Oak Ridges—Richmond Hill]], crosses the floor to join the [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservatives]], citing concerns for the Liberal's handling of the economy, foreign and security policies, and international trade.<ref name="AlleslevCBC" />
*September 30, 2018: [[Peter Van Loan]], Conservative MP for [[York—Simcoe (federal electoral district)|York—Simcoe]] resigns his seat in the House of Commons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Honourable Peter Van Loan – Overview – House of Commons of Canada |url=https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/25465?name=Van-Loan,-Peter-(Hon) |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803021424/https://www.ourcommons.ca/Parliamentarians/en/members/25465?name=Van-Loan%2C-Peter-(Hon) |archive-date=August 3, 2019 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=ourcommons.ca}}</ref>
*November 7, 2018: [[Parry Sound—Muskoka (federal electoral district)|Parry Sound-Muskoka]] MP [[Tony Clement]] resigns from the [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative]] caucus, at the request of leader Andrew Scheer, due to a [[sexting]] scandal.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Boutilier |first=Alex |date=November 7, 2018 |title=Clement booted from Conservative caucus over sexting scandal |work=Toronto Star |url=https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2018/11/07/clement-booted-from-conservative-caucus-over-sexting-scandal.html |access-date=November 7, 2018 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202818/https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2018/11/07/clement-booted-from-conservative-caucus-over-sexting-scandal.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
*November 30, 2018: [[Brampton East (federal electoral district)|Brampton East]] MP [[Raj Grewal]] resigns from the [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal]] caucus to enter treatment due to a [[gambling addiction]].<ref name="grewal" /><ref name="GrewalCBC" />

===2019===
*January 2, 2019: [[Sheila Malcolmson]], NDP MP for [[Nanaimo—Ladysmith]] resigned her seat to seek election in the British Columbia provincial riding of [[Nanaimo (provincial electoral district)|Nanaimo]].<ref name="Malcolmson" />
*January 17, 2019: As no other candidate had entered the race by the January 15 nomination deadline, [[Yves-François Blanchet]] was [[2019 Bloc Québécois leadership election|acclaimed leader]] of the [[Bloc Québécois]].<ref name="BlanchetWins" />
*January 29, 2019: [[Nicola Di Iorio]], Liberal MP for [[Saint-Léonard—Saint-Michel]] resigned his seat in the House of Commons.<ref name="Di Iorio" />
*February 10, 2019: [[Scott Brison]], Liberal MP for [[Kings—Hants]] resigned his seat in the House of Commons.<ref name="Brison" />
*February 25, 2019: By-elections were held in [[Outremont (electoral district)|Outremont]], [[York—Simcoe (federal electoral district)|York—Simcoe]] and [[Burnaby South]], electing Liberal [[Rachel Bendayan]], Conservative [[Scot Davidson]], and New Democrat [[Jagmeet Singh]], respectively.
*March 20, 2019: [[Whitby (federal electoral district)|Whitby]] MP [[Celina Caesar-Chavannes]] resigned from the Liberal caucus.<ref name="Chavannes" />
*April 2, 2019: [[Markham—Stouffville (federal electoral district)|Markham—Stouffville]] MP [[Jane Philpott]] and [[Vancouver Granville]] MP [[Jody Wilson-Raybould]] were removed from the Liberal caucus.<ref name="PhilpottJWR" />
*May 6, 2019: A by-election was held in [[Nanaimo—Ladysmith]], electing Green candidate [[Paul Manly]].<ref name="Manly" />
*June 20, 2019: [[Mark Warawa]], Conservative MP for [[Langley—Aldergrove]] died of cancer.<ref name="Warawa">{{Cite web |last=Tunney |first=Catharine |date=June 20, 2019 |title=B.C. MP Mark Warawa dies after 'valiant battle' with cancer |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/mark-warawa-dead-cancer-1.5182705 |access-date=June 21, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202823/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/mark-warawa-dead-cancer-1.5182705 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*August 2, 2019: [[Deepak Obhrai]], Conservative MP for [[Calgary Forest Lawn]] died from liver cancer.<ref name="Obhrai">{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2019 |title=Long-time Conservative MP Deepak Obhrai has died at age 69 |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/long-time-conservative-mp-deepak-obhrai-has-died-at-age-69-1.5235730 |access-date=August 3, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=August 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190803171318/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/long-time-conservative-mp-deepak-obhrai-has-died-at-age-69-1.5235730 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* August 16, 2019: [[Pierre Nantel]] was removed from the [[New Democratic Party]] caucus and de-selected as the NDP candidate for [[Longueuil—Saint-Hubert]] after reports surfaced of ongoing discussions regarding Nantel joining the [[Green Party of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wherry |first=Aaron |date=August 16, 2019 |title=Elizabeth May says she has been in talks with ejected NDP MP for 'some considerable time' |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/pierre-nantel-out-1.5250128 |access-date=May 3, 2021 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202823/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/pierre-nantel-out-1.5250128 |url-status=live }}</ref> He announces that he is now an independent MP.
* August 19, 2019: [[Pierre Nantel]] repeated that he will remain an independent MP until the end of his term in the current Parliament and announces that he will be a candidate for the [[Green Party of Canada]] in the election for the next Parliament.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gilmore |first=Rachel |title=Former NDP MP Pierre Nantel joins the Green Party |work=CTV News |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/former-ndp-mp-pierre-nantel-joins-the-green-party/ |access-date=August 19, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202820/https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/former-ndp-mp-pierre-nantel-joins-the-green-party-1.4555929 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="NantelClarified">{{Cite news |date=August 19, 2019 |title=Pierre Nantel passe au Parti Vert |language=fr |work=Le Soleil |agency=La Presse Canadienne |url=https://www.lesoleil.com/actualite/politique/pierre-nantel-passe-au-parti-vert-30a51d2451a301faba83aa0a3636d259 |access-date=August 20, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202834/https://www.lesoleil.com/actualite/politique/pierre-nantel-passe-au-parti-vert-30a51d2451a301faba83aa0a3636d259 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*September 10, 2019: The [[Rhinoceros Party]] nominated a candidate named Maxime Bernier in [[Beauce (electoral district)|Beauce]], the riding of [[People's Party of Canada|People's Party]] leader [[Maxime Bernier]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Elliott |first=Josh K. |date=September 11, 2019 |title=PPC Leader Maxime Bernier to face another Maxime Bernier in his riding |work=Global News |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5887668/2-maxime-bernier-candidates-rhinoceros/ |access-date=September 15, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202845/https://globalnews.ca/news/5887668/2-maxime-bernier-candidates-rhinoceros/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* September 11, 2019: [[Dissolution of parliament|Parliament is dissolved]] and [[Dropping the writ|writs of election are dropped]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tunney |first=Catharine |date=September 11, 2019 |title=It's official, Canadians: the 2019 federal election campaign is underway |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/election-campaign-starts-today-1.5277657 |access-date=September 11, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=November 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111185038/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/election-campaign-starts-today-1.5277657 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*September 13, 2019: Elizabeth May announced that her party will conduct more thorough "re-vetting" of candidates after media reports of some Green candidates have made past statements opposing legal abortion.<ref name="green-quebec">{{Cite web |last=Tasker |first=John Paul |date=September 13, 2019 |title=Elizabeth May says Green party is 're-vetting' candidates after anti-abortion comments come to light |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/green-party-re-vetting-candidates-abortion-quebec-1.5282892 |access-date=September 14, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210310/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/green-party-re-vetting-candidates-abortion-quebec-1.5282892 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*September 15, 2019: Andrew Scheer said he will stand by candidates despite "controversial" comments in the past as long as the candidate apologizes, and takes responsibility for said comments.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1173085469409546240 |user=CBCKatie |title=Scheer says he will stand by candidates despite controversial comments in the past (including racist, and homophobic comments) as long as the candidate apologizes, and takes responsibility for said comments. He says each situation will depend on context though. |author=Katie Simpson |date=2019-09-15 |access-date=2021-02-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1173195801457283074 |user=CBCPolitics |title=Conservative Leader Andrew Scheer says he will stand by candidates with racist, homophobic past comments as long as they apologize. https://t.co/CSLM18sKir #hw #cdnpoli #elxn43 https://t.co/7NwmocvjQr |date=2019-09-15 |access-date=2021-02-06}}</ref>
*September 16, 2019: Maxime Bernier was officially invited to the debates organized by the [[Leaders' Debates Commission]] after Commissioner David Johnston announces the People's Party meets the criteria set for the debates.<ref name="MBinvited">{{Cite news |last=Wherry |first=Aaron |date=September 16, 2019 |title=Maxime Bernier invited to participate in official commission debates |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/maxime-bernier-debates-commission-election-1.5285162 |access-date=September 16, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202825/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/maxime-bernier-debates-commission-election-1.5285162 |url-status=live }}</ref>
*October 11–14, 2019: Advance polls were open, with an estimated record 4.7&nbsp;million electors casting their ballots, a turnout increase of 29% above the [[2015 Canadian federal election|2015 general election]]. It also marked the first time polls have been open for 12 hours each day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 15, 2019 |title=Estimate of Turnout at Advance Polls Now Available |url=https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=med&document=oct1519&dir=pre&lang=e |access-date=October 16, 2019 |publisher=Elections Canada |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202848/https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=med&document=oct1519&dir=pre&lang=e |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=First Estimate of Turnout at Advance Polls |url=https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=med&dir=bkg&document=ge43_turnout&lang=e |access-date=October 19, 2019 |website=elections.ca |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202911/https://www.elections.ca/content.aspx?section=med&dir=bkg&document=ge43_turnout&lang=e |url-status=live }}</ref>
*October 18, 2019: Elections Canada reports historic turnout among international voters, with 21,842 electors casting their ballots.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Slaughter |first=Graham |date=October 18, 2019 |title=Elections Canada reports historic turnout among international voters |url=https://election.ctvnews.ca/elections-canada-reports-historic-turnout-among-international-voters-1.4645263 |access-date=October 19, 2019 |website=CTV News |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202849/https://election.ctvnews.ca/elections-canada-reports-historic-turnout-among-international-voters-1.4645263 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*October 21, 2019: Election Day: The Liberal Party, led by incumbent Prime Minister [[Justin Trudeau]], forms a minority government with 157 seats.

==Election campaign==
===Liberal===
The [[Parliament of Canada]]'s [[Ethics Commissioner (Canada)|Ethics Commissioner]], [[Mario Dion]], found that Trudeau improperly influenced then [[Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada|Minister of Justice and Attorney General]] [[Jody Wilson-Raybould]] to intervene in an ongoing criminal case against Quebec-based construction company [[SNC-Lavalin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tunney |first=Catherine |date=August 14, 2019 |title=RCMP looking at SNC-Lavalin affair 'carefully,' promise to take actions 'as required' |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/rcmp-snc-report-examining-carefully-1.5247119 |access-date=August 16, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=August 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814233921/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/rcmp-snc-report-examining-carefully-1.5247119 |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[29th Canadian Ministry|Trudeau government]] has maintained that there was no undue pressure or law broken, that offering SNC-Lavalin a [[Deferred prosecution agreement (Canada)|deferred prosecution agreement]] (DPA) could save jobs, and that the controversy resulted from a misunderstanding and an "erosion of trust". [[SNC-Lavalin affair|The affair]] became public in February 2019, shortly after Wilson-Raybould had been shuffled to another cabinet position. Wilson-Raybould resigned from cabinet later that day. This was followed by the resignation of cabinet minister [[Jane Philpott]], over the government's handling of the affair. In April, Wilson-Raybould and Philpott were expelled by Trudeau from the Liberal caucus; Trudeau cited concerns for division in and subsequent weakening of the Liberal party. On April 2, 2019, Wilson-Raybould, as Liberal candidate for [[Vancouver Granville]], and Philpott, as Liberal candidate for [[Markham—Stouffville (federal electoral district)|Markham—Stouffville]], were deselected as candidates.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Vigliotti |first1=Marco |last2=Pinkerton |first2=Charlie |last3=Johnson |first3=Kelsey |date=April 2, 2019 |title=Jody Wilson-Raybould, Jane Philpott removed from Liberal caucus |url=https://ipolitics.ca/2019/04/02/jody-wilson-raybould-jane-philpott-removed-from-liberal-caucus/ |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=iPolitics |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203616/https://ipolitics.ca/2019/04/02/jody-wilson-raybould-jane-philpott-removed-from-liberal-caucus/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In late August, Party deputy leader [[Ralph Goodale]], Liberal candidate for [[Regina—Wascana]], [[Lawrence MacAulay]], candidate for [[Cardigan (electoral district)|Cardigan]], and [[Francis Scarpaleggia]], candidate for [[Lac-Saint-Louis (electoral district)|Lac-Saint-Louis]], were singled out for their opposition to [[same-sex marriage]]. Pundits argued that Goodale was being hypocritical, due to his role with Scheer and the same-sex marriage incident.<ref>{{Cite news |last=DiManno |first=Rosie |date=August 24, 2019 |title=Rosie DiManno: Liberals should be ashamed for dredging up Andrew Scheer same-sex marriage speech |work=The Hamilton Spectator |url=https://www.thespec.com/opinion-story/9565115-rosie-dimanno-liberals-should-be-ashamed-for-dredging-up-andrew-scheer-same-sex-marriage-speech/ |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203604/https://www.thespec.com/opinion/contributors/2019/08/24/rosie-dimanno-liberals-should-be-ashamed-for-dredging-up-andrew-scheer-same-sex-marriage-speech.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Selley |first=Chris |date=August 23, 2019 |title=Chris Selley: Goodale's same-sex-marriage gambit is staggeringly arrogant and hypocritical |url=https://nationalpost.com/opinion/chris-selley-goodales-same-sex-marriage-gambit-is-staggeringly-arrogant-and-hypocritical |website=National Post |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203555/https://nationalpost.com/opinion/chris-selley-goodales-same-sex-marriage-gambit-is-staggeringly-arrogant-and-hypocritical |url-status=live }}</ref> Goodale later stated that he had evolved on the position and wanted answers from Scheer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White-Crummey |first=Arthur |date=August 23, 2019 |title='I too have evolved': Goodale wants clarity from Scheer on LGBTQ positions |url=https://leaderpost.com/news/saskatchewan/i-too-have-evolved-goodale-wants-clarity-from-scheer-on-lgbtq-positions |website=Regina Leader-Post |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203606/https://leaderpost.com/news/saskatchewan/i-too-have-evolved-goodale-wants-clarity-from-scheer-on-lgbtq-positions |url-status=live }}</ref>

On August 30, Hassan Guillet, Liberal candidate for [[Saint-Léonard—Saint-Michel]], was dropped as a candidate following allegations of anti-Semitic comments from [[B'nai B'rith]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zimonjic |first=Peter |date=August 30, 2019 |title=Liberals dump Quebec candidate after B'nai Brith, Conservatives allege anti-Semitic comments Social Sharing concern that his ethnicity would be out of place in the majority Italian riding.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pirro |first=Raphael |date=June 12, 2019 |title=Saint-Léonard: un ex-député libéral outré par la candidature d'un non-Italien |url=https://www.lapresse.ca/actualites/politique/201906/11/01-5229805-saint-leonard-un-ex-depute-liberal-outre-par-la-candidature-dun-non-italien.php |url-status=live }}</ref> Guillet denied the allegation, alleged that the Liberals were aware of the post, and that they "imposed" his replacement [[Patricia Lattanzio]], on the riding.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lévesque |first=Catherine |date=September 10, 2019 |title=Montreal city councillor replaces former imam Hassan Guillet as Liberal candidate |url=https://montrealgazette.com/news/local-news/montreal-city-councillor-replaces-former-imam-hassan-guillet-as-liberal-candidate |website=The Gazette |location=Montreal |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203614/https://montrealgazette.com/news/national/election-2019/montreal-city-councillor-replaces-former-imam-hassan-guillet-as-liberal-candidate?r |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 20, Guillet announced he would run as an independent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rowe |first=Daniel J. |date=September 22, 2019 |title=Hassan Guillet to run as an |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203646/https://montreal.ctvnews.ca/hassan-guillet-to-run-as-an-independent-in-st-leonard-1.4604785 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Sameer Zuberi, Liberal candidate for [[Pierrefonds—Dollard]], was nominated on September 15, despite questioning Osama bin Laden's involvement in 9/11 in a social media post.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Sameer Zuberi chosen as Liberal candidate for Pierrefonds-Dollard |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/sameer-zuberi-pierrefonds-dollard-1.5286997 |access-date=September 21, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203610/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/sameer-zuberi-pierrefonds-dollard-1.5286997 |url-status=live }}</ref> Zuberi called the accusations false saying it was an attempt by the Conservatives to deflect attention away from their own candidates with extremist or white supremacist leanings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arnold |first=Janice |date=September 18, 2019 |title=Liberals stand by Montreal candidate accused of 'anti-Semitic past' |url=https://www.cjnews.com/news/canada/liberals-stand-by-montreal-candidate-accused-of-anti-semitic-past |access-date=September 21, 2019 |website=The Canadian Jewish News |archive-date=September 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921222824/https://www.cjnews.com/news/canada/liberals-stand-by-montreal-candidate-accused-of-anti-semitic-past |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 18, ''L'Express of Drummondville'' reported that the Liberal candidate for [[Drummond (federal electoral district)|Drummond]], William Morales' nomination victory was attended by two convicted criminals. Morales said that while he maintains contact with Spanish-speaking members from the Drummondville community the two people were not involved in his campaign and he does not have close relations with them.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Levesque |first=Fanny |date=September 18, 2019 |title=Des invités gênants pour un candidat libéral |url=https://www.lapresse.ca/elections-federales/201909/18/01-5241812-des-invites-genants-pour-un-candidat-liberal.php |website=La Presse |language=fr |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203639/https://www.lapresse.ca/elections-federales/2019-09-18/des-invites-genants-pour-un-candidat-liberal |url-status=live }}</ref> He later told his local newspaper that he interacts with members regardless of their background.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aubin |first=Erika |date=September 25, 2019 |title=William Morales explique sa version des faits |url=https://www.journalexpress.ca/2019/09/25/william-morales-explique-sa-version-des-faits/ |website=LeXpresse |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706203631/https://www.journalexpress.ca/2019/09/25/william-morales-explique-sa-version-des-faits/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 23, Del Arnold, Liberal candidate for [[Calgary Shepard]], apologized to Conservative rival [[Tom Kmiec]] after spreading misleading information about his place of residence. Arnold has not apologized for a deleted tweet that accused Andrew Scheer of having links to "white supremacy" and the 2017 [[Unite the Right rally]] in Virginia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bellemare |first=Andrea |date=September 26, 2019 |title=Calgary Liberal candidate apologizes for misleading leaflets attacking Conservative opponent |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/liberal-attacks-conservative-candidate-1.5297446 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=May 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210504035133/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/liberal-attacks-conservative-candidate-1.5297446 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 28, [[Judy Sgro]], Liberal candidate for [[Humber River—Black Creek (federal electoral district)|Humber River—Black Creek]], made remarks during an interview with a radio network called GBKM FM defending Trudeau's wearing of brownface/blackface makeup: "Those in the black community have told me how much more love they have for the prime minister, that he wanted to have a black face. That he took great pride in that, too". She later apologized for her remarks, saying that "the comments I made on GBKM FM were insensitive," and further adding "I should have known better, and I apologize".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Joanna |date=October 9, 2019 |title=Liberal Judy Sgro sorry for 'insensitive' comments about Trudeau's blackface |url=https://nationalpost.com/pmn/news-pmn/canada-news-pmn/liberal-judy-sgro-sorry-for-insensitive-comments-about-trudeaus-blackface |access-date=October 11, 2019 |website=National Post |archive-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210809032246/https://nationalpost.com/pmn/news-pmn/canada-news-pmn/liberal-judy-sgro-sorry-for-insensitive-comments-about-trudeaus-blackface |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Walsh |first1=Marieke |last2=Kirkup |first2=Kristy |date=October 9, 2019 |title=Liberal candidate Judy Sgro apologizes for 'insensitive' blackface remarks |work=The Globe and Mail |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-liberal-candidate-judy-sgro-apologizes-for-insensitive-blackface-2/ |access-date=October 11, 2019 |archive-date=October 11, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191011120027/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-liberal-candidate-judy-sgro-apologizes-for-insensitive-blackface-2/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Andrea |first=Aaron |date=October 9, 2019 |title=Toronto Liberal candidate Judy Sgro's 'blackface' comments appall local activists |url=https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/10/09/toronto-liberal-candidate-judy-sgro-apologizes-for-insensitive-comments-about-trudeaus-blackface.html |access-date=October 11, 2019 |website=The Star |archive-date=October 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191010112951/https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/10/09/toronto-liberal-candidate-judy-sgro-apologizes-for-insensitive-comments-about-trudeaus-blackface.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 13, due to a security threat, Trudeau appeared 90 minutes late to a campaign rally. Trudeau took extraordinary security precautions at the event. He wore a bulletproof vest and was surrounded by heavily armed security personnel. His wife was also supposed to introduce him, but she did not appear on stage. The Liberal Party did not reveal the nature of the threat.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Berthiaume |first=Lee |date=October 12, 2019 |title=Trudeau wears protective vest after security concern delays Liberal rally in Toronto |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/6026732/trudeau-security-vest-rally-toronto-concern/ |access-date=October 13, 2019 |website=Global News |archive-date=October 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013153813/https://election.ctvnews.ca/trudeau-appeared-at-rally-in-bulletproof-vest-amid-security-concern-1.4636483 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=October 12, 2019 |title=Trudeau wears bulletproof vest after security threat delays campaign rally |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-wears-bulletproof-vest-after-security-threat-delays-campaign-rally-1.5319730 |access-date=October 13, 2019 |archive-date=October 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013000158/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-wears-bulletproof-vest-after-security-threat-delays-campaign-rally-1.5319730 |url-status=live }}</ref> Scheer and Singh both showed concern for Trudeau following the threat.<ref name="Slaughter-2019" /><ref name="CBC-2019">{{Cite news |date=October 13, 2019 |title=Trudeau vows campaign won't change course after threat forced him to wear bulletproof vest |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-scheer-singh-security-threat-bulletproof-vest-1.5319859 the RCMP was still with the Liberal leader.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1183476752514985989 |user=glen_mcgregor |title=These guys are RCMP ERT officers. They are *not* CF Rangers, although the logo on their shirts is similar. |author=Glen McGregor |date=2019-10-13 |access-date=2021-02-06}}</ref> Furthermore, Trudeau explained that he followed advice from the RCMP and that this event will not change the way he campaigns.<ref name="CBC-2019" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Turnbull |first=Sarah |date=October 13, 2019 |title=Trudeau says security threat won't change how he campaigns |url=https://election.ctvnews.ca/trudeau-says-security-threat-won-t-change-how-he-campaigns-1.4636812 |access-date=October 13, 2019 |website=CTV News |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706205550/https://election.ctvnews.ca/trudeau-says-security-threat-won-t-change-how-he-campaigns-1.4636812 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 14, Trudeau dodged multiple questions about a possible coalition with the NDP in a minority scenario. He responded that he remains focused on winning a majority.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bryden |first=Joan |date=October 14, 2019 |title=Trudeau dodges question of Liberal-NDP coalition while Scheer rallies against |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/6030766/liberal-ndp-coalition-election/ |access-date=October 14, 2019 |website=Global News |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706205552/https://globalnews.ca/_static/?%3F-eJx9jksKAjEQRC9k0ioamYV4lkzSaDQ%2FUh3E25sBFyrisqDeq6J7Va5k4SyUuqqxn0MGXVmqdTc16R2l4ntkUONohb2qBfKVtANW9FsFts1daNQhwdXGAPkAocF8WtQcy9iEPMacTiH%2F074%2FXEyvvCCndNyY7X5tJnMwT2WAUrI= |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Tunney-2019">{{Cite news |last=Tunney |first=Catharine |date=October 14, 2019 |title=Singh distances himself from coalition talk as campaign enters final week |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-coalition-ndp-windsor-1.5320394 |access-date=October 14, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706205527/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/trudeau-coalition-ndp-windsor-1.5320394 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Conservative===

On July 10, Cyma Musarat, Conservative candidate for [[Pickering—Uxbridge]], faced an allegation from fellow party members that she won her nomination by using improper voting procedures.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dillon |first=Moya |date=July 10, 2019 |title=Pickering-Uxbridge Conservatives split over federal nomination |url=https://www.durhamregion.com/news-story/9494514-pickering-uxbridge-conservatives-split-over-federal-nomination/ |access-date=September 3, 2019 |website=DurhamRegion.com |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706205606/https://www.durhamregion.com/news-story/9494514-pickering-uxbridge-conservatives-split-over-federal-nomination/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Conservative Party faced an accusation that its headquarters had been delaying the nomination contest to find a different candidate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rana |first=Abbas |date=March 25, 2019 |title=Former Ontario Conservative MP Chisu to run as a People's Party candidate in upcoming election |url=https://www.hilltimes.com/2019/03/25/disappointed-former-ontario-conservative-mp-chisu-leaves-party-will-run-as-a-peoples-party-candidate-in-the-upcoming-election/193688 |access-date=September 3, 2019 |website=The Hill Times |archive-date=November 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191114185110/https://www.hilltimes.com/2019/03/25/disappointed-former-ontario-conservative-mp-chisu-leaves-party-will-run-as-a-peoples-party-candidate-in-the-upcoming-election/193688 |url-status=live }}</ref> From July 24 to September 15, Ghada Melek attracted attention. This conservative candidate for [[Mississauga—Streetsville (federal electoral district)|Mississauga—Streetsville]], was revealed by former organizers of the [[Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario|Ontario Progressive Conservative Party]] to have been rejected as a candidate in the [[Mississauga—Streetsville (provincial electoral district)|provincial riding]] over [[Twitter]] posts about Muslim extremism.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Blackwell |first=Tom |date=July 24, 2019 |title=Her run for the Ontario PCs ended after she tweeted about Islam, but Ghada Melek is now a federal Conservative candidate |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/the-ontario-pcs-rejected-her-over-her-tweets-about-islam-but-ghada-melek-is-now-a-federal-conservative-candidate |access-date=September 3, 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[National Council of Canadian Muslims]] had issues over Melek's Twitter posts about Islam and LGBT+ community.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keri |first=Been |date=August 5, 2019 |title=Muslim group calls on Conservative candidate to step down over social media posts |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5721380/ghada-melek-conservative-candidate/ |access-date=April 23, 2021 }}</ref> Scheer accepted an apology she issued for her comments.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cornwell |first=Steve |date=September 13, 2019 |title=Scheer on the defensive over past anti-LGBTQ posts by Mississauga and Brampton Conservative candidates |url=https://www.bramptonguardian.com/news-story/9595526-scheer-on-the-defensive-over-past-anti-lgbtq-posts-by-mississauga-and-brampton-conservative-candidates/ |website=bramptonguardian.com |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> Later, CTV News obtained her provincial vetting report and her promotion of conspiracy theories was seen as another factor behind her disqualification.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aiello |first=Rachel |date=September 14, 2019 |title=Tory candidate Scheer defended deemed 'extremely controversial and problematic' in 2016 vetting report |url-status=dead }}</ref> When asked about the provincial party red-flagging Melek, Scheer defended her again.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1173094932879265793 |user=omarsachedina |title=I asked Scheer On August 22, Scheer faced questions over a 2005 online video in which he spoke against same-sex marriage<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boutilier |first=Alex |date=August 22, 2019 |title=Andrew Scheer urged to end 'boycott' of gay pride events after 2005 speech on same-sex marriage comes to light |url=https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/08/22/andrew-scheer-said-gay-couples-lack-inherent-quality-of-marriage-in-tape-of-2005-speech-unearthed-by-liberals.html |access-date=September 15, 2019 |website=Toronto Star |location=Ottawa |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210038/https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/08/22/andrew-scheer-said-gay-couples-lack-inherent-quality-of-marriage-in-tape-of-2005-speech-unearthed-by-liberals.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Scheer himself did not respond until a press conference a week later where he argued that Trudeau was raising a wedge issue;<ref>{{Cite news |last=Harris |first=Kathleen |date=August 29, 2019 |title=Scheer accuses Trudeau of whipping up divisive social issues to distract from scandals |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/andrew-scheer-social-controversy-conservative-1.5264360 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210044/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/andrew-scheer-social-controversy-conservative-1.5264360 |url-status=live }}</ref> Several pundits had an issue with his response.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teitel |first=Emma |date=August 31, 2019 |title=On the subject of gay marriage, why can't Andrew Scheer show a little humanity? |url=https://www.thestar.com/opinion/star-columnists/2019/08/31/on-the-subject-of-gay-marriage-why-cant-andrew-scheer-show-a-little-humanity.html |access-date=September 15, 2019 |website=Toronto Star |archive-date=September 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190913220753/https://www.thestar.com/opinion/star-columnists/2019/08/31/on-the-subject-of-gay-marriage-why-cant-andrew-scheer-show-a-little-humanity.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Paez |first=Beatrice |date=September 4, 2019 |title=Scheer's ambiguous positioning on abortion, gay rights a ripe way to lose Red Tories, say politicos |url=https://www.hilltimes.com/2019/09/04/scheers-ambiguous-positioning-on-abortion-gay-rights-a-ripe-way-to-lose-red-tories-say-politicos/213397 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |website=The Hill Times |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210233/https://www.hilltimes.com/2019/09/04/scheers-ambiguous-positioning-on-abortion-gay-rights-a-ripe-way-to-lose-red-tories-say-politicos/213397 |url-status=live }}</ref> Weeks later, Scheer was asked if he needed to apologize for his comments giving the standards he set for his candidates; however he gave no response.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1173299506064035847 |user=CBCKatie |title=Asked Scheer if he needs to apologize for comments in made in 2005 on same sex marriage, given the framework he's set out for candidates and their past controversial comments. He does not apologize. |date=September 15, 2019 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |last=Simpson |first=Katie}}</ref> After Trudeau's apology regarding blackface, Scheer was asked again if he should apologize for his words; he gave no response.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1175025181116514304 |user=althiaraj |title=Scheer says Trudeau is not living up to his own standard. Scheer twice sidesteps questions about whether he is sorry he compared same-sex marriage to a dog's tail. Actually, that is three times. |date=September 20, 2019 |access-date=September 20, 2019 |last=Raj |first=Althia}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1174708641758359553 |user=CBCKatie |title=Scheer is asked if he should apologize for his same sex marriage speech in 2005. He doesn't. Says the conversation today is about Trudeau. This is the second time specifically he's been asked if he wants to apologize during the campaign. |date=September 19, 2019 |access-date=September 20, 2019 |last=Simpson |first=Katie}}</ref> Scheer once again chose to not answer the question directly on popular Quebec talk show {{lang|fr|[[Tout le monde en parle (Canadian talk show)|Tout le monde en parle]]}}. He said that he supports the law and the rights of Canadians, but that he will not walk in Pride parades.<ref name="Raj-2019">{{Cite web |last=Raj |first=Althia |date=September 30, 2019 |title=Scheer Defends Climate Plan, Says He Won't Walk in Pride Parades As PM |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/andrew-scheer-pride-climate_ca_5d9208c8e4b0ac3cddac1a01 |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=HuffPost |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210305/https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/andrew-scheer-pride-climate_ca_5d9208c8e4b0ac3cddac1a01 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Between August 26 and 30, the Conservatives were questioned on abortion. [[Alain Rayes]], Scheer's [[Quebec lieutenant]], attracted attention after he told a Quebec radio station that he misspoke on the party stance on abortion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Raj |first=Althia |date=August 26, 2019 |title=Scheer's Top Quebec MP Admits To Giving The Wrong Impression on Abortion |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/alain-rayes-scheer-abortion_ca_5d646465e4b0641b2551c23d |access-date=September 15, 2019 |website=HuffPost |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210232/https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/alain-rayes-scheer-abortion_ca_5d646465e4b0641b2551c23d |url-status=live }}</ref> A few days later, Scheer held a press conference, where he addressed the issue. However, his answers were seen as confusing in the media, and anti-abortion activists found his answers to be mixed-messaging.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wherry |first=Aaron |date=August 30, 2019 On September 12, Rachel Wilson, Conservative candidate for [[York Centre (federal electoral district)|York Centre]], attracted attention after a video was posted online that called for pro-life legislation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maloney |first=Ryan |date=September 12, 2019 |title=Scheer Blasts Liberals For Sharing Video Targeting Anti-Abortion Candidate |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/andrew-scheer-rachel-willson-abortion-rights_ca_5d7a6802e4b0fc7153436c14 |access-date=September 14, 2019 |website=HuffPost |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210234/https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/andrew-scheer-rachel-willson-abortion-rights_ca_5d7a6802e4b0fc7153436c14 |url-status=live }}</ref> Wilson did not comment when asked about abortion legislation.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1172160496570699778 |user=AbigailBimman |title=Conservative candidate @rachelbwillson was asked several times if she would introduce abortion legislation. On September 28, ''The Globe and Mail'' revealed that they found no record of Scheer receiving the licence required by law to work as an insurance agent or broker in Saskatchewan despite him claiming so in the past.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Clark |first1=Campbell |last2=Radwanski |first2=Adam |date=September 28, 2019 |title=Andrew Scheer, a work in progress: Where the Conservative Leader comes from and how he really thinks |work=The Globe and Mail |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-andrew-scheer-a-work-in-progress-where-the-conservative-leader-comes/ |access-date=October 16, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210236/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-andrew-scheer-a-work-in-progress-where-the-conservative-leader-comes/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=von Scheel |first=Elise |date=September 29, 2019 |title=Liberals ask for an investigation of Scheer's insurance industry credentials |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/andrew-scheer-insurance-broker-accreditation-1.5302093 |access-date=October 16, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210235/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/andrew-scheer-insurance-broker-accreditation-1.5302093 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="McGregor-2019">{{Cite news |last=McGregor |first=Janyce |date=September 30, 2019 |title=Andrew Scheer's experience in the insurance industry: '6 or 7 months' |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/scheer-insurance-broker-monday-1.5303394 |access-date=October 16, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210239/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/scheer-insurance-broker-monday-1.5303394 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Robert Fife]], the Ottawa bureau chief for ''The Globe and Mail'', explained that Scheer was an insurance clerk.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CTV QP: Was Andrew Scheer an insurance broker? |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/video/?clipId=1792338&cache=/ |access-date=October 16, 2019 |website=CTV News |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210236/https://www.ctvnews.ca/video?clipId=1792338&cache= |url-status=live }}</ref> Scheer responded by saying that he did receive his accreditation, but that he left the insurance office before the licensing process was finalized.<ref name="McGregor-2019" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 30, 2019 |title=Scheer accused of falsely claiming he was once an insurance broker in Saskatchewan |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5968537/scheer-insurance-broker-claim/ |access-date=October 16, 2019 |website=Global News |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210223/https://globalnews.ca/news/5968537/scheer-insurance-broker-claim/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Later, the Insurance Brokers Association of Saskatchewan said that Scheer completed just one of four required courses to become an insurance broker. On October 3, ''The Globe and Mail'' revealed that Scheer had [[Dual citizenship|dual]] Canadian and American citizenship.
