On October 11, the CBC filed an application in the Federal Court of Canada against the Conservative party over the use of television excerpts in partisan advertising. They claimed the party's use of excerpts violated the "moral rights" of news anchor Rosemary Barton and reporter John Paul Tasker. The action was brought despite the material having been taken down from websites and deleted from Twitter. The CBC said that it was given no reassurance that such use would not be repeated. The lawsuit says that the use of the material in a partisan way "diminishes the reputation" of the CBC and leaves it open to allegations that it is biased.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Leblanc |first1=Daniel |last2=Houpt |first2=Simon |date=October 11, 2019 |title=CBC and Rosemary Barton take Conservatives to court over election ads |work=The Globe and Mail |location=Ottawa |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-cbc-and-rosemary-barton-take-conservatives-to-court-over-election-ads/ |access-date=October 12, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210230/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-cbc-and-rosemary-barton-take-conservatives-to-court-over-election-ads/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Higgins |first=Michael |date=October 11, 2019 |title=CBC sues the Conservative party over copyright, 'moral rights' of journalists |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/election-2019/cbc-sues-the-conservative-party-over-copyright-journalists-moral-rights |access-date=October 12, 2019 |website=National Post |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210221/https://nationalpost.com/news/politics/election-2019/cbc-sues-the-conservative-party-over-copyright-journalists-moral-rights |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=October 12, 2019 |title=CBC taking Conservative Party to court over online election ad |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/cbc-conservative-party-lawsuit-1.5319209 |access-date=October 12, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210249/https://www.cbc.ca/news/cbc-conservative-party-lawsuit-1.5319209 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1183042040256516097 |user=RosieBarton |title=CBC has issued this statement about its legal filing |date=October 12, 2019 |access-date=October 12, 2019 |last=Barton |first=Rosemary}}</ref>

=== New Democratic Party ===
NDP candidates were dropped or stepped down during the course of the campaign. On June 20, Rana Zaman, candidate for [[Dartmouth—Cole Harbour]], was dropped over comments about the [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]] that the party deemed "unacceptable".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benjamin |first=Graeme |date=June 20, 2019 |title=NDP part ways with Dartmouth-Cole Harbour candidate over 'recently surfaced tweets' |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5413069/ndp-part-ways-with-zaman/ |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=[[Global News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210241/https://globalnews.ca/wp-content/themes/shaw-globalnews/assets/dist/css/critical-tablet-portrait.css?m=1625604668g |url-status=live }}</ref>

On August 16, [[Pierre Nantel]], candidate for [[Longueuil—Saint-Hubert]], was de-selected after reports surfaced of ongoing discussions regarding Nantel joining the [[Green Party of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gilmore |first=Rachel |date=August 19, 2019 |title=Former NDP MP Pierre Nantel joins the Green Party |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/former-ndp-mp-pierre-nantel-joins-the-green-party/ |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=[[CTV News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706202820/https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/former-ndp-mp-pierre-nantel-joins-the-green-party-1.4555929 |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 11, Dock Currie, candidate for [[Kamloops—Thompson—Cariboo|Kamloops-Thompson-Cariboo]], was forced to resign over "flippant and aggressive" comments he made toward pro-pipeline activists.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weichel |first=Andrew |date=September 11, 2019 |title=NDP candidate dropped over social media spat with pro-pipeline activists |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/ndp-candidate-dropped-over-social-media-spat-with-pro-pipeline-activists/ |access-date=September 12, 2019 |website=bc.ctvnews.ca |location=Vancouver |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210235/https://bc.ctvnews.ca/ndp-candidate-dropped-over-social-media-spat-with-pro-pipeline-activists-1.4588764 |url-status=live }}</ref> The next day, Olivier Mathieu, candidate for [[LaSalle—Émard—Verdun|Lasalle-Emard-Verdun]], stepped down following allegations of physical abuse against his ex-spouse.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kovac |first=Adam |date=September 12, 2019 |title=Montreal-area NDP candidate withdraws over domestic violence allegations |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/montreal/article/montreal-area-ndp-candidate-withdraws-over-domestic-violence-allegations/ |access-date=September 12, 2019 |website=montreal.ctvnews.ca |location=Montreal |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210243/https://montreal.ctvnews.ca/montreal-area-ndp-candidate-withdraws-over-domestic-violence-allegations-1.4589799 |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the election, Jagmeet Singh has faced questions about wearing of a turban and whether that would reduce the number of people who would vote for him. Jonathan Richardson, the former federal NDP's executive member for Atlantic Canada, who defected to the [[Green Party of Canada|Green Party]], stated in an interview with [[CBC Radio]], that some potential NDP candidates were hesitant to run in New Brunswick, due to Singh's turban.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodyear |first=Sheena |date=September 4, 2019 |title=NDP defector says he warned party some N.B. voters are 'uncomfortable' with Jagmeet Singh |url=https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-wednesday-edition-1.5270097/ndp-defector-says-he-warned-party-some-n-b-voters-are-uncomfortable-with-jagmeet-singh-1.5270101 |website=CBC Radio |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210300/https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-wednesday-edition-1.5270097/ndp-defector-says-he-warned-party-some-n-b-voters-are-uncomfortable-with-jagmeet-singh-1.5270101 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[CTV News]] covered a Singh event in [[Verner, Ontario]] and spoke to a number of voters there, including NDP supporters, who said that they would not vote for a leader wearing a turban.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergeron Oliver |first=Annie |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Some voters question whether Canada is ready for a PM with a turban |url=https://election.ctvnews.ca/some-voters-question-whether-canada-is-ready-for-a-pm-with-a-turban-1.4598227 |website=CTV News |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210252/https://election.ctvnews.ca/some-voters-question-whether-canada-is-ready-for-a-pm-with-a-turban-1.4598227 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[CBC News]] found a similar reaction in [[Ruth Ellen Brosseau]]'s riding.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1174346197764587522 |user=CBCTheNational |title=She didn't campaign and she didn't live in the riding, but riding the orange wave in 2011, she won and was re-elected in 2015—@RosieBarton talks to NDP MP Ruth Ellen Brosseau about running for her third mandate and the challenges her party faces in Quebec. |date=September 18, 2019 |access-date=September 24, 2019}}</ref> Singh responded to these concerns. He explained some things about his turban and recorded a French ad without it to alleviate people's worries.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thibedeau |first=Hannah |date=September 16, 2019 |title=5 things Jagmeet Singh wants you to know about his turban |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/singh-list-turban-questions-ndp-1.5284388 |access-date=September 24, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210323/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/singh-list-turban-questions-ndp-1.5284388 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lao |first=David |date=September 15, 2019 |title=Jagmeet Singh wanted to 'show an openness' to Quebec with ad displaying him without a turban |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5906436/jagmeet-singh-quebec-ndp-ad-bill21/ |access-date=September 24, 2019 |website=[[Global News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210248/https://globalnews.ca/news/5906436/jagmeet-singh-quebec-ndp-ad-bill21/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Furthermore, according to [[Alexandre Boulerice]], the party's Deputy Leader and [[Quebec lieutenant]], the NDP is targeting young voters and they do not care about the turban.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Marquis |first1=Melanie |last2=Bellavance |first2=Joel-Denis |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Le plan d'attaque des partis |url=https://www.lapresse.ca/actualites/politique/201908/30/01-5239347-le-plan-dattaque-des-partis.php |access-date=September 24, 2019 |website=La Presse |language=fr |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210230/https://www.lapresse.ca/actualites/politique/2019-08-31/le-plan-d-attaque-des-partis |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 2, a man told Singh to cut off his turban to look more Canadian during a campaign stop. Singh replied that Canadians "look like all sorts of people" before walking off.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 2, 2019 |title=Jagmeet Singh: 'Cut your turban off,' voter tells NDP leader |publisher=BBC |agency=The Canadian Press |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-49901451 |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210259/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-49901451 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=October 2, 2019 |title=Jagmeet Singh challenges man who urged him to 'cut off' his turban |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/jagmeet-singh-ndp-montreal-turban-sikh-1.5305840 |access-date=October 10, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210249/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/jagmeet-singh-ndp-montreal-turban-sikh-1.5305840 |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the campaign, Singh talked about what he would do in a minority. On August 22, due to the controversy over Scheer's previous comments about same-sex marriage, he announced that the NDP would not support a Conservative minority government under any circumstances.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gilmore |first=Rachel |date=August 22, 2019 |title=Singh would not support Conservatives if NDP holds the balance of power after fall election |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/singh-would-not-support-conservatives-if-ndp-holds-the-balance-of-power-after-fall-election-1.4561260?cache= |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=[[CTV News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210242/https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/singh-would-not-support-conservatives-if-ndp-holds-the-balance-of-power-after-fall-election-1.4561260?cache= |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 22, Singh announced that despite Trudeau's past brownface and blackface incidents, he would not rule out working with the Liberals in a minority scenario.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aiello |first=Rachel |date=September 22, 2019 |title=Despite Trudeau doing brownface, Singh hasn't ruled out working with Liberals in minority scenario |url=https://election.ctvnews.ca/despite-trudeau-doing-brownface-singh-hasn-t-ruled-out-working-with-liberals-in-minority-scenario-1.4604765 |access-date=September 22, 2019 |website=Federal Election 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210323/https://election.ctvnews.ca/despite-trudeau-doing-brownface-singh-hasn-t-ruled-out-working-with-liberals-in-minority-scenario-1.4604765 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On October 10, he laid out the conditions for NDP support in a minority Parliament: a national single-payer universal pharmacare plan, a national dental care plan, investments in housing, a plan to waive interest on student loans, a commitment to reduce emissions, to end subsidies for oil companies and to deliver aid to oilpatch workers to transition them out of fossil fuel industries, the introduction of a "super wealth" tax, a commitment to closing tax loopholes and reducing cellphone bills. He later added that changing the way the country votes is also a condition (Singh's NDP backs a system of [[mixed-member proportional representation]]).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tunney |first=Catherine |date=October 10, 2019 |title=NDP Leader Jagmeet Singh begins to lay out minority scenario priorities |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/ndp-singh-priorities-minority-1.5315981 |access-date=October 10, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210253/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/ndp-singh-priorities-minority-1.5315981 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2019 |title=Priorities to pumpkin patches: Federal party leaders have light day on campaign trail ahead of French debate |url=https://edmonton.citynews.ca/2019/10/10/federal-leaders-light-day-campaign-french-debate/ |access-date=October 10, 2019 |website=City News |location=Ottawa |agency=NEWS 1130 Staff and The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210302/https://edmonton.citynews.ca/2019/10/10/federal-leaders-light-day-campaign-french-debate/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He added that he does not rule out supporting a pipeline-owning Liberal minority government.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wherry |first=Aaron |date=October 11, 2019 |title=Singh doesn't rule out supporting a pipeline-owning Liberal minority government |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/jagmeet-singh-minority-government-trans-mountain-1.5317466 |access-date=October 11, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210308/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/jagmeet-singh-minority-government-trans-mountain-1.5317466 |url-status=live }}</ref> On October 13, Singh said he would "do whatever it takes" to keep the Tories from power, including forming a coalition government with the Liberals. He added that he is "ready to work with anyone", when he was asked about the Bloc.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Raj |first=Althia |date=October 13, 2019 |title=Singh Will Push For Coalition Government If Tories Fall Shy of Majority |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/jagmeet-singh-coalition_ca_5da39506e4b02c9da04c8656 |access-date=October 14, 2019 |website=HuffPost |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210248/https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/jagmeet-singh-coalition_ca_5da39506e4b02c9da04c8656 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rabson web |last=Cousins |first=Ben |date=October 14, 2019 |title=Singh downplays prospect of a coalition, saying 'vote for a New Democrat' |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/federal-election-2025/ |access-date=October 14, 2019 |website=CTV News |archive-date=July 6, 2021 ===Bloc Québécois===
On August 9, André Parizeau, Bloc candidate for [[Ahuntsic-Cartierville (electoral district)|Ahuntsic-Cartierville]], created attention over his past communist affiliations as Leader of the Parti communiste du Québec (PCQ).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lévesque |first=Catherine |date=August 9, 2019 |title=André Parizeau will be Bloc candidate in Ahuntsic-Cartierville |url=https://montrealgazette.com/news/local-news/bloc-leader-says-he-can-tolerate-communists-but-not-racists-and-xenophobes |access-date=April 24, 2021 |website=The Gazette |location=Montreal |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210251/https://montrealgazette.com/news/local-news/bloc-leader-says-he-can-tolerate-communists-but-not-racists-and-xenophobes |url-status=live }}</ref> Parizeau disavowed the PCQ in order to be accepted as candidate.<ref>{{Citation |last=Paré |first=Étienne |title=L'ancien chef du Parti communiste sera finalement candidat pour le Bloc |date=August 16, 2019 |url=https://www.journaldemontreal.com/2019/08/16/le-chef-du-bloc-quebecois-lance-un-ultimatum-a-un-candidat-controverse-1 |place=Montreal |language=fr |access-date=September 12, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210243/https://www.journaldemontreal.com/2019/08/16/le-chef-du-bloc-quebecois-lance-un-ultimatum-a-un-candidat-controverse-1 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In October, the Bloc Québécois called on Quebeckers to vote for candidates "who resemble you" (" des gens qui nous ressemblent ") in the election, prompting NDP Leader Jagmeet Singh to denounce the message as unacceptable and divisive. In his closing statement during Wednesday's French-language debate, Bloc Leader Yves-François Blanchet called on voters to "opt for men and women who resemble you, who share your values, who share your concerns and who work for your interests, and only for the interests of Quebeckers." The Bloc has said the comment has nothing to do with someone's background or religion but with Québécois values.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ballingall |first=Alex |date=October 3, 2019 |title=Bloc Québécois blasted for urging voters to support candidates 'qui vous ressemblent' |url=https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/10/03/bloc-qubcois-blasted-for-urging-voters-to-support-candidates-qui-vous-ressemblent.html |access-date=April 24, 2021 |website=The Star |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210256/https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/10/03/bloc-qubcois-blasted-for-urging-voters-to-support-candidates-qui-vous-ressemblent.html ===Green Party ===
Several GPC candidates were dropped or stepped down during the course of the campaign. On July 23, Brock Grills, Green candidate for [[Peterborough—Kawartha]], stepped down for "personal reasons". Grills was accused of fraud by a former employer but he and the EDA president stated that accusation was not the reason behind his stepping down. Grills, who repeated his reasoning, also mentioned the Green Party central office "pushed" for his resignation because he was reaching out to other parties to ask them to adopt policies to curb climate change.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Nyznik |first1=Jessica |last2=Kovach |first2=Joelle |date=August 17, 2019 |title=Former Green party candidate says he didn't step down over fraud accusations |url=https://www.thepeterboroughexaminer.com/news-story/9553924-former-green-party-candidate-says-he-didn-t-step-down-over-fraud-accusations/ |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=ThePeterboroughExaminer.com |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210251/https://www.thepeterboroughexaminer.com/news/peterborough-region/2019/08/17/former-green-party-candidate-says-he-didn-t-step-down-over-fraud-accusations.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On August 16, Luc Saint-Hilaire, Green candidate for [[Lévis—Lotbinière]], was forced to resign because of a Facebook post demanding Boufeldja Benabdallah, co-founder of the [[Centre Culturel Islamique de Québec]], to denounce a man who allegedly lit his ex-wife on fire.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ballingall |first=Alex |date=August 16, 2019 |title=Green candidate forced to resign after criticizing mosque leader |url=https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/08/16/green-candidate-forced-to-resign-after-criticizing-mosque-leader.html |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=Toronto Star |location=Ottawa |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210314/https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/08/16/green-candidate-forced-to-resign-after-criticizing-mosque-leader.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 12, Erik Schomann, Green candidate for [[Simcoe North (federal electoral district)|Simcoe North]], resigned over a 2007 Facebook post which appeared to suggest he wanted to mail pieces of a pig carcass to Muslims in support of the protesters during the [[Jyllands-Posten Muhammad cartoons controversy|Muhammed comic controversy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Connolly |first=Amanda |date=September 12, 2019 |title=Green Party candidate resigns over post about mailing pig carcass to Muslims |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5893499/green-party-pig-carcass/ |website=Global News 7, Marthe Lépine, candidate in [[Glengarry—Prescott—Russell (federal electoral district)|Glengarry—Prescott—Russell]], was dropped over anti-abortion comments; however, as the party missed the deadline to remove her from the ballot, she remained despite being disavowed.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Tunney|first=Catharine|date=October 7, 2019|title=Green Party drops anti-abortion candidate in Ontario riding|work=[[CBC News]]|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/green-party-glengarry-prescott-russell-abortion-1.5311705|access-date=November 8, 2021}}</ref>

On September 9, the Green Party issued a statement insisting that there is "zero chance" of reopening the abortion debate; few hours after May stated the Green Party will not ban members from trying to reopen abortion debate in an interview.<ref>{{Cite news |last=MacDonald |first=Brennan |date=September 9, 2019 |title=Green Party won't ban members from trying to reopen abortion debate, says May |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/powerandpolitics/green-party-elizabeth-may-abortion-debate-1.5273722 |access-date=September 16, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210339/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/powerandpolitics/green-party-elizabeth-may-abortion-debate-1.5273722 |url-status=live }}</ref> May later added that MPs risk being ousted if they move to reopen the debate.<ref>{{Cite news |last=May |first=Elizabeth |date=September 9, 2019 |title=Elizabeth May clarifies position on abortion, says Green Party screens out candidates who disagree |work=The Globe and Mail |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-elizabeth-may-clarifies-position-on-abortion-says-green-party-screens/ |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210323/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-elizabeth-may-clarifies-position-on-abortion-says-green-party-screens/ |url-status=live }}</ref> From September 10 to 16, attention was focused on [[Pierre Nantel]], the candidate for [[Longueuil—Saint-Hubert]]. He created this attention over his comments about [[Quebec sovereignty movement|Québec separatism]] on a Quebec radio station. May disputed that Nantel was a [[Quebec sovereigntist]], but Nantel contradicted her afterwards.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tasker |first=John Paul |date=September 12, 2019 |title='Of course I'm a sovereignist,' Green candidate says after Elizabeth May insists he's not |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/pierre-nantel-green-party-sovereigntist-1.5281661 |access-date=September 17, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210311/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/pierre-nantel-green-party-sovereigntist-1.5281661 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, May stated he could be still be a candidate.<ref name="green-quebec" /> Some journalists and columnists were confused by her reasoning for keeping him as a candidate.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1172640795142307841 |user=RosieBarton |title=If May wants to keep him as a candidate that's fine, but this reasoning is nonsensical and is frankly ridiculous. The sovereigntist movement's primary goal is to separate. |date=September 13, 2019 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |last=Barton |first=Rosemary}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1172800233782333441 |user=ChantalHbert |title=Sérieusement ??? |date=September 14, 2019 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |language=fr |last=Hébert |first=Chantal}}</ref> Furthermore, May was asked by the son of the late [[Jack Layton]] to not use the latter for political points when defending Nantel.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paling |first=Emma |date=September 16, 2019 |title=Jack Layton's Son Asks May To Stop Invoking His Dad For 'Political Points' |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/mike-layton-elizabeth-may-jack-name_ca_5d7fe760e4b00d69059d0c06 |access-date=September 18, 2019 |website=HuffPost |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210305/https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/mike-layton-elizabeth-may-jack-name_ca_5d7fe760e4b00d69059d0c06 |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 10, Mark Vercouteren, the candidate for [[Chatham-Kent—Leamington (federal electoral district)|Chatham-Kent-Leamington]], and Macarena Diab, the candidate for [[Louis-Hébert (federal electoral district)|Louis-Hébert]] were revealed to have made "anti-abortion statements".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tasker |first=John Paul |date=September 10, 2019 |title=Green candidates say they don't remember past anti-abortion comments |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/green-party-anti-abortion-candidates-1.5277682 |publisher=CBC News |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210328/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/green-party-anti-abortion-candidates-1.5277682 |url-status=live }}</ref> A spokesperson defended both of them but a few days later, it was revealed by May that Vercoutern was being "re-vetted" over the party not noticing Vercouteren's questionnaires.<ref name="green-quebec"/> A week after the original comments were revealed, Vercouteren stated his view aligned with the party.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Chatham-Kent-Leamington Green party candidate clarifies position on abortion |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210316/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/windsor/chatham-kent-leamington-green-party-candidate-clarifies-abortion-position-1.5286220 |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 12, Dale Dewar, Green candidate for [[Regina—Qu'Appelle]], apologized for making past negative comments on social media about Israel, [[Zionism]] and [[Israelis]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 13, 2019 |title=Strongly worded posts by Regina Green candidate decried by Holocaust studies group |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/saskatchewan/dale-dewar-green-party-1.5282368 |access-date=September 14, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |location=Saskatchewan |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 6, 2021 On October 15, the Green Party found anti-Islam social-media posts by four of its Quebec candidates.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 15, 2019 |title=Four Green nominees in Quebec made Islamophobic comments, party says |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/four-green-candidates-islamophobic-comments-1.5321883 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |location=Montreal |agency=The Canadian Press |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210309/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/four-green-candidates-islamophobic-comments-1.5321883 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 15, 2019 |title=4 Quebec Green Party Candidates To Apologize For Islamophobic Comments |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/green-party-quebec-islamophobic_ca_5da64d95e4b002e33e7698cf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191022064755/https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/entry/green-party-quebec-islamophobic_ca_5da64d95e4b002e33e7698cf |archive-date=October 22, 2019 |access-date=October 22, 2019 |website=[[HuffPost]] |location=Ottawa |agency=The Canadian Press}}</ref>
 
Starting on September 23, the GPC drew scrutiny around the world for manipulating a picture of Elizabeth May to make it seem as if she was using a reusable cup and metal straw instead of a disposable cup.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Forrest |first1=Maura |last2=Thomson |first2=Stuart |date=September 23, 2019 |title=Green Party used Photoshop to add reusable cup and metal straw to photo of Elizabeth May |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Cecco |first=Leyland |date=September 25, 2019 |title=Canada's Green Party alters photo of leader using single-use cup |work=The Guardian Leading up to and during the campaign, May talked about what she would do in a minority. On September 3, she announced that she would not be prepared to prop up any minority government of the major parties given current climate plans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gilmore |first=Rachel |date=September 3, 2019 |title=May: Greens won't support any minority government given current climate plans |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/may-greens-wont-support-any-minority-government-given-current-climate-plans/ |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=[[CTV News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210328/https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/may-greens-won-t-support-any-minority-government-given-current-climate-plans-1.4576188 |url-status=live }}</ref> Later, on September 26, May announced that the GPC would not prop up a minority government that moves forward with the Trans Mountain pipeline expansion.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thurton |first=David |date=September 26, 2019 |title=Greens wouldn't support a minority government that moves to build the Trans Mountain pipeline |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/may-minority-pipeline-support-1.5297700 |access-date=September 26, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210304/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/may-minority-pipeline-support-1.5297700 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the final week of the campaign, the idea of a coalition took hold. May said that in countries with [[proportional representation]], parties can plan to govern together before the election, but that in Canada such talk is "meaningless" due to the [[First-past-the-post voting|first-past-the-post]] system.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 17, 2019 |title=Discuter de coalition est " prématuré ", dit Elizabeth May |url=https://www.lapresse.ca/elections-federales/201910/17/01-5245807-discuter-de-coalition-est-premature-dit-elizabeth-may.php |access-date=October 19, 2019 |website=La Presse |language=fr |agency=La Presse Canadienne |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210348/https://www.lapresse.ca/elections-federales/2019-10-17/discuter-de-coalition-est-premature-dit-elizabeth-may |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2019 |title=Green Leader Elizabeth May calls talk of a coalition government 'premature' |url=https://election.ctvnews.ca/green-leader-elizabeth-may-calls-talk-of-a-coalition-government-premature-1.4643369 |access-date=October 19, 2019 |website=CTV News |location=Qualicum Beach, B.C. |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210335/https://election.ctvnews.ca/green-leader-elizabeth-may-calls-talk-of-a-coalition-government-premature-1.4643369 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== People's Party ===

|url-status=live }}</ref> One of those founding members—a former American neo-Nazi leader—was volunteering for the party. He was also a member of the [[Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario|Ontario Progressive Conservative Party]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Picazo |first=Alheli |date=August 30, 2019 |title=Maxime Bernier Should Have Known A Neo-Nazi Was Working For His Party |work=Canadaland |url=https://www.canadalandshow.com/maxime-bernier-should-have-known-a-neo-nazi-was-working-for-his-party/ |access-date=September 25, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210422/https://www.canadaland.com/maxime-bernier-should-have-known-a-neo-nazi-was-working-for-his-party/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was removed from the party on August 29, after his past came to light.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Prévost |first=Hugo |date=August 29, 2019 |title=Le Parti populaire du Canada coupe les ponts avec un organisateur au lourd passé |language=fr |work=Radio Canada |url=https://ici.radio-canada.ca/nouvelle/1279961/politique-parti-populaire-organisateur-neonazi |access-date=September 25, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210336/https://ici.radio-canada.ca/nouvelle/1279961/politique-parti-populaire-organisateur-neonazi |url-status=live }}</ref> The PPC's spokesperson said that it did not come up during the vetting process since he came from the US. On July 30, Cody Payant, People's candidate for [[Carlton Trail—Eagle Creek]], attracted attention for a social media post defending [[Lindsay Shepherd]]. Payant argue that it was taken out of context. Bernier defended Payant after he spoke to Payant and was satisfied with his explanation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White-Crummey |first=Arthur |date=July 30, 2019 |title=Bernier defends Sask. candidate who urged 'more hate speech' |url=https://leaderpost.com/news/saskatchewan/bernier-defends-sask-candidate-who-urged-more-hate-speech |website=Regina Leader-Post |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210425/https://leaderpost.com/news/saskatchewan/bernier-defends-sask-candidate-who-urged-more-hate-speech |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 2, Maxime Bernier called [[Greta Thunberg]] "mentally unstable" on Twitter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Breen |first=Kerri |date=September 2, 2019 |title=Maxime Bernier calls teen climate activist 'mentally unstable' – National |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5846043/maxime-bernier-greta-thunberg-mentally-unstable/ |access-date=September 18, 2019 |website=[[Global News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210428/https://globalnews.ca/_static/?%3F-eJx9jksKAjEQRC9k0ioamYV4lkzSaDQ%2FUh3E25sBFyrisqDeq6J7Va5k4SyUuqqxn0MGXVmqdTc16R2l4ntkUONohb2qBfKVtANW9FsFts1daNQhwdXGAPkAocF8WtQcy9iEPMacTiH%2F074%2FXEyvvCCndNyY7X5tJnMwT2WAUrI= |url-status=live }}</ref> A few days later, he backtracked his comments stating his intention was to criticize her role as "a spokesperson for [[Media coverage of global warming|climate alarmism]]" and did not mean to denigrate her.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ferreras |first=Jesse |date=September 4, 2019 |title=After labelling Greta Thunberg 'mentally unstable,' Maxime Bernier calls her 'brave' |work=Global News |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5857679/maxime-bernier-greta-thunberg-mentally-unstable-brave/ |access-date=September 17, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210324/https://globalnews.ca/news/5857679/maxime-bernier-greta-thunberg-mentally-unstable-brave/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After the campaign, Bernier classified these comments as his only election regret and as a mistake.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dawson |first=Tyler |date=November 18, 2019 |title=Maxime Bernier has one election regret, but says he's definitely running again |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/maxime-bernier-has-one-election-regret-but-says-hes-definitely-running-again |access-date=November 19, 2019 |website=National Post |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210434/https://nationalpost.com/news/maxime-bernier-has-one-election-regret-but-says-hes-definitely-running-again?r |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 18, [[Steven Fletcher (politician)|Steven Fletcher]], People's candidate for [[Charleswood—St. James—Assiniboia—Headingley]], denied allegations for illegally using campaign signs and voter data from the Conservative Party. Fletcher also suggested that the move was political motivated from the Conservative and took issues to the fact that the letter was leaked online.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Khan |first=Ahmar |date=September 18, 2019 |title=People's Party candidate Steven Fletcher accused of taking voter data from Conservatives |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/steven-fletcher-electinon-data-1.5287147 |access-date=September 18, 2019 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210407/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/steven-fletcher-electinon-data-1.5287147 |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 19, 2019, Nancy Mercier, People's candidate for [[Beauséjour (electoral district)|Beauséjour]], raised concern from local organizations over comments about [[Islamism]] and [[immigration]] Mercier indicated her concerns are with Islamic terrorism and not members of any race.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 19, 2019 |title=People's Party candidate in Beauséjour faces criticism for 'racist' comments |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/new-brunswick/nancy-mercier-beausejour-people-s-party-immigration-racist-1.5288289 |access-date=September 20, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210433/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/new-brunswick/nancy-mercier-beausejour-people-s-party-immigration-racist-1.5288289 |url-status=live }}</ref> On October 10, Sybil Hogg, the candidate for Sackville-Preston-Chezzetcook, came under fire for a series of [[Islamophobia|anti-Islam]] tweets calling Islam "pure evil" and for the religion to be banned in Canada. The PPC's executive director reached out to her to understand the context and Hogg explained that she failed to draw the distinction between "Islam" and "Islamism" or "radical Islam". She added that her concern was radical Islam and not Islam. Due to the response, the PPC said they would not take action against her. Later, Bernier called the tweets "absolutely racist and Islamophobic" and confirmed that she will not face consequences.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benjamin |first=Graeme |date=October 10, 2019 |title=Halifax-area PPC candidate under fire for Islamophobic tweets |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/6016116/sybil-hogg-islam-tweets/ |access-date=October 12, 2019 |website=Global News |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210349/https://globalnews.ca/news/6016116/sybil-hogg-islam-tweets/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=October 10, 2019 |title=People's Party won't take action against N.S. candidate who called Islam 'pure evil' |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/peoples-party-nova-scotia-hogg-bernier-islam-social-media-posts-1.5315943 |access-date=October 12, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210328/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/peoples-party-nova-scotia-hogg-bernier-islam-social-media-posts-1.5315943 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2019 |title='Absolutely, yes:' Bernier confirms Nova Scotia PPC candidate's tweets were racist |url=https://globalnews.ca/video/6025126/absolutely-yes-bernier-confirms-nova-scotia-ppc-candidates-tweets-were-racist/ |access-date=October 12, 2019 |website=Global News |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210346/https://globalnews.ca/_static/?%3F-eJytlUFOxDAMRS9EWkBQsUEsuABX8CRua5HYVexMNZyeqCMhsWTMoqrU+j+5%2FzvuuG8hChuyjbZiQR11hT0sWU6QGXcdo%2FZLOIKNLLVApi8cMp2GQjz0l3fjnxhzr9QBcr5RfwKl6NBfn3o6yHCRZg7ARtFaxZk64XYjC6iniYLcHHLqd4+JEao0xdwlpQj%2FB8kQFKuDpCb1EoqkltFjTYEFj3ogdjVEnDshqFH8vIQzJRQHzSpyIl48Dm09damYHAyxOUDyzI7tZOYydu6LzNPBJl16u3yVXhAromfuvePwc268oEP%2F0beiK5K2JTB8l8a+aFUigSec6%2FGtsnvmo+kalBZum+dXFwNxOLaSg1IhkSfeQx9mEWcurZ7x13e8ldeH6fF5un+appdvsDI3UQ=%3D |url-status=live }}</ref>

Several candidates were dropped or stepped down before the election. On September 6, Ken Pereira, People's candidate for [[Portneuf—Jacques-Cartier]], stepped down because of a "terrible family tragedy". When announced as the candidate, Pereira had attracted attention for his online "anti-vaccine" and "pro-conspiracy theory" posts and was defended by the party.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Laframboise |first=Kalina |date=September 6, 2019 |title=Ken Pereira will not run for People's Party of Canada |work=Global News |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5866264/ken-pereira-drops-out-from-peoples-party-of-canada/ |access-date=September 12, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210353/https://globalnews.ca/_static/?%3F-eJx9jksKAjEQRC9k0ioamYV4lkzSaDQ%2FUh3E25sBFyrisqDeq6J7Va5k4SyUuqqxn0MGXVmqdTc16R2l4ntkUONohb2qBfKVtANW9FsFts1daNQhwdXGAPkAocF8WtQcy9iEPMacTiH%2F074%2FXEyvvCCndNyY7X5tJnMwT2WAUrI= |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 12, Brian Misera, People's candidate for [[Coquitlam—Port Coquitlam]], claimed that he was removed for asking Bernier to denounce racism more clearly in an online video posted on Misera's Twitter account. However, the PPC stated that Misera was removed after he allegedly admitted to the party that he was his own financial agent, a violation of [[Elections Canada]] rules.<ref name="OttCit20190913">{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Joanna |date=September 13, 2019 |title=Party leaders contend with posts and past lives from candidates in campaign |url=https://ottawacitizen.com/pmn/news-pmn/canada-news-pmn/leaders-link-up-with-their-political-families-for-day-3-of-federal-campaign/wcm/899931a3-e0bf-475a-811e-fe445fe63faa |website=Ottawa Citizen |agency=The Canadian Press |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210310/https://ottawacitizen.com/pmn/news-pmn/canada-news-pmn/leaders-link-up-with-their-political-families-for-day-3-of-federal-campaign/wcm/899931a3-e0bf-475a-811e-fe445fe63faa |url-status=live }}</ref> Yet a statement of Misera's disqualification obtained by City News made no reference to the PPC's claim or Misera's claim.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boothby |first=Lauren |date=September 12, 2019 |title=PPC ousts candidate who asks Bernier to denounce racism in ranks |url=https://edmonton.citynews.ca/2019/09/12/ppc-racism-candidate/ |access-date=September 24, 2019 |website=CityNews Edmonton |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210353/https://edmonton.citynews.ca/2019/09/12/ppc-racism-candidate/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 30, Chad Hudson, People's Party candidate for the Nova Scotia riding of West Nova, tweeted that he would no longer be running for the party, less than two hours before Elections Canada's deadline for candidates to officially register to be on the ballot. He criticized the party and its leadership for being "divisive", as well as "bad for democracy" and contributors to the "toxic state of politics". Hudson, later admitted that he did not notify the party of his decision.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pinkerton |first=Charlie |date=September 30, 2019 |title=PPC candidate quits, says party's 'divisive' and Bernier's using 'dark and dangerous' tactics |url=https://ipolitics.ca/2019/09/30/ppc-candidate-quits-says-partys-divisive-and-berniers-using-dark-and-dangerous-tactics/ |access-date=April 24, 2021 |website=iPolitics |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210434/https://ipolitics.ca/2019/09/30/ppc-candidate-quits-says-partys-divisive-and-berniers-using-dark-and-dangerous-tactics/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On October 8, Victor Ong, the People's Party of Canada candidate in Winnipeg North, resigned after deciding the party is "racist and intolerant".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rollason |first=Kevin |date=October 8, 2019 |title=Winnipeg North PPC candidate ends run for 'racist, intolerant' party |work=Winnipeg Free Press |url=https://www.winnipegfreepress.com/special/federal-election/son-of-asian-immigrants-ends-candidacy-for-racist-intolerant-party-562561712.html |access-date=October 10, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210311/https://www.winnipegfreepress.com/special/federal-election/son-of-asian-immigrants-ends-candidacy-for-racist-intolerant-party-562561712.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lorange |first=Simon-Olivier |date=October 9, 2019 |title=Un autre candidat du Parti populaire claque la porte |url=https://www.lapresse.ca/elections-federales/201910/09/01-5244767-un-autre-candidat-du-parti-populaire-claque-la-porte.php |access-date=October 10, 2019 |website=La Presse |language=fr |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210400/https://www.lapresse.ca/elections-federales/2019-10-09/un-autre-candidat-du-parti-populaire-claque-la-porte |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Third-party organizations ===
On August 19, environmental groups were warned by [[Elections Canada]] that any third party that promotes information about climate change during the election period with paid advertising could be engaging in partisan activity.<ref name="BBC">{{Cite news |date=August 19, 2019 |title=Why Canadians won't see ads about climate change |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-49400492 |access-date=August 19, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210447/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-49400492 |url-status=live }}</ref> Registered charities with a charitable tax status would be required to register as a third party for the election if they engaged in any partisan activity incurring $500, which would include advertising and surveys, or risk their charitable tax status.<ref name="CBC_20190819">{{Cite news |date=August 19, 2019 |title=Environmental groups warned that saying climate change is real could be seen as partisan |publisher=[[CBC News]] |agency=The Canadian Press |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/environment-groups-warned-climate-change-real-partisan-1.5251763 |access-date=August 9, 2021 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210329/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/environment-groups-warned-climate-change-real-partisan-1.5251763 |url-status=live }}</ref> These regulations were a result of [[People's Party of Canada]] leader [[Maxime Bernier]] expressing doubts about the legitimacy of climate change, because a third party that advertises the dangers of climate change during the election period may be considered to be indirectly advocating against the People's Party.<ref name="CBC_20190819" /> After confusion about the warning, Elections Canada released a public statement to clarify that the prohibition applied only to advertising, not speech in general the following day.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Zimonjic |first=Peter |date=August 20, 2019 |title=Environmental groups can still talk climate change during election, says Canada's chief electoral officer |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/climate-elections-canada-perrault-1.5253580 |access-date=August 20, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210317/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/climate-elections-canada-perrault-1.5253580 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On August 25, billboards purchased by a True North Strong & Free Advertising Corp., a third party promoting the [[People's Party of Canada]]'s immigration policy, with the text "Say NO to Mass Immigration" appeared in Vancouver, Calgary, Regina, and Halifax. True North Strong & Free Advertising Corp is run by Frank Smeenk, the chief executive of a Toronto-based mining exploration company. The Peoples Party of Canada told the media that it had no contact with the group.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Paas-Lang |first=Christian |date=August 23, 2019 |title=Third party buys billboard to promote Bernier's immigration stance |agency=The Canadian Press |location=Ottawa |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-third-party-buys-billboard-to-promote-maxime-berniers-anti-mass/ |access-date=September 1, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210437/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/politics/article-third-party-buys-billboard-to-promote-maxime-berniers-anti-mass/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Initially, [[Pattison Outdoor Advertising]] defended the billboards, arguing that they complied with the [[Advertising Standards Canada]] Code<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cosh |first=Colby |date=August 27, 2019 |title=Colby Cosh: How a 'leftist mob' handed Mad Max a pre-election gift |url=https://nationalpost.com/opinion/colby-cosh-how-a-leftist-mob-handed-mad-max-a-pre-election-gift |access-date=September 1, 2019 |website=National Post |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210351/https://nationalpost.com/opinion/colby-cosh-how-a-leftist-mob-handed-mad-max-a-pre-election-gift |url-status=live }}</ref> but later decided to pull them and said that they would review their protocols on advocacy advertising.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Joanna |date=August 26, 2019 |title=Third-party advertiser disavows 'mass immigration' message on billboards |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5814496/maxime-bernier-billboard-woes/ |access-date=September 1, 2019 |website=[[Global News]] |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210347/https://globalnews.ca/_static/?%3F-eJx9jksKAjEQRC9k0ioamYV4lkzSaDQ%2FUh3E25sBFyrisqDeq6J7Va5k4SyUuqqxn0MGXVmqdTc16R2l4ntkUONohb2qBfKVtANW9FsFts1daNQhwdXGAPkAocF8WtQcy9iEPMacTiH%2F074%2FXEyvvCCndNyY7X5tJnMwT2WAUrI= |url-status=live }}</ref> The Pattison president later revealed that the billboards would have stayed up had True North Strong & Free identified themselves on the billboards and how the public could get in touch with them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Joanna |date=August 27, 2019 |title=Billboard company 'appalled' no one taking ownership of Bernier ads |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/article/billboard-company-appalled-no-one-taking-ownership-of-bernier-ads/ |access-date=September 1, 2019 |website=[[CTV News]] |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210319/https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/billboard-company-appalled-no-one-taking-ownership-of-bernier-ads-1.4567399 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 3, the CBC revealed that the [[Manning Centre]] is a driving financial force behind a network of anti-Liberal Facebook pages pumping out political messaging and memes during the federal election campaign.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Paas-Lang |first=Christian |date=October 3, 2019 |title=Manning Centre a primary backer for series of anti-Liberal Facebook pages |publisher=[[CBC News]] |agency=The Canadian Press |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/manning-centre-proud-1.5307111 |access-date=October 18, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210359/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/manning-centre-proud-1.5307111 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Livesey |first=Bruce |date=October 17, 2019 |title=Andrew Scheer: Big Oil's secret weapon |url=https://www.nationalobserver.com/2019/10/17/analysis/andrew-scheer-big-oils-secret-weapon |access-date=October 18, 2019 |website=National Observer |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210427/https://www.nationalobserver.com/2019/10/17/analysis/andrew-scheer-big-oils-secret-weapon |url-status=live }}</ref> Facebook pulled one of their ads due to the excess violence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maher |first=Stephen |date=October 12, 2019 |title=The 'excessively violent' election ad, paid for by the Manning Centre |url=https://www.macleans.ca/politics/ottawa/the-excessively-violent-election-ad-paid-for-by-the-manning-centre/ |access-date=October 18, 2019 |website=Maclean's |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210501/https://www.macleans.ca/politics/ottawa/the-excessively-violent-election-ad-paid-for-by-the-manning-centre/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Manning Centre's donations to those groups, worth more than $300,000, are hidden, since the think tank, which did not register as a third party, does not intend to disclose them. Elections Canada says there is nothing in the law to prevent outside groups from raising money and then passing those donations along to third-party advertisers.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Keller |first1=James |last2=Cryderman |first2=Kelly |date=October 15, 2019 |title=Manning Centre won't disclose source of donations to third parties for attack ads on Liberals |work=The Globe and Mail |location=Calgary |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-manning-centre-wont-disclose-source-of-donations-to-third-parties-for/ |access-date=October 18, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210335/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-manning-centre-wont-disclose-source-of-donations-to-third-parties-for/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McIntosh |first=Emma |date=October 17, 2019 |title=Explainer: The rise of Canada's right-wing meme pages |url=https://www.nationalobserver.com/2019/10/17/analysis/explainer-rise-canadas-right-wing-meme-pages |access-date=October 18, 2019 |website=National Observer |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210432/https://www.nationalobserver.com/2019/10/17/analysis/explainer-rise-canadas-right-wing-meme-pages |url-status=live }}</ref> As a result of this lack of disclosure, [[Democracy Watch (Canada)|Democracy Watch]] filed a complaint to Canada's [[Chief Electoral Officer (Canada)|chief electoral officer]]. It argued that the Manning Centre should have registered as a third party.<ref name="Carman-2019"/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Beland |first=Gabriel |date=October 17, 2019 |title=Le groupe de pression Québec Fier visé par une plainte électorale |url=https://www.lapresse.ca/elections-federales/201910/17/01-5245805-le-groupe-de-pression-quebec-fier-vise-par-une-plainte-electorale.php |access-date=October 18, 2019 |website=La Presse |language=fr |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210331/https://www.lapresse.ca/elections-federales/2019-10-17/le-groupe-de-pression-quebec-fier-vise-par-une-plainte-electorale |url-status=live }}</ref> Furthermore, due to this controversy, [[Jean-Pierre Kingsley]], the former chief electoral officer, said that the next federal government must close the gap in the law that allowed the Manning Centre to raise money and then pass it along to third-party groups without disclosing the source of those donations.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Keller |first=James |date=October 16, 2019 |title=Former chief electoral officer calls for next federal government to close loophole in third-party donation law |work=The Globe and Mail |location=Calgary |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/alberta/article-former-chief-electoral-officer-calls-for-next-federal-government-to/ |access-date=October 18, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210400/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/alberta/article-former-chief-electoral-officer-calls-for-next-federal-government-to/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

* Eliminate subsidies for fossil fuel businesses.<ref name="newsinteractives.cbc.ca">{{Cite news |title=How do the main parties compare on these issues? |publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |url=https://newsinteractives.cbc.ca/elections/federal/2019/party-platforms/ |access-date=2021-08-09 |archive-date=2020-03-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200318211932/https://newsinteractives.cbc.ca/elections/federal/2019/party-platforms/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Misinformation ==
During the Maclean's debate, Scheer said that refugees were "jumping the queue". Journalists called this a false statement and one expert explained that "there is no queue".<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 13, 2019 |title=Reality check: Scheer's claim about refugees 'jumping the queue' is false – National |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5899144/reality-check-scheer-immigration-refugee-queue-jumping/ |access-date=September 14, 2019 |website=[[Global News]] |last1=Hill |first1=Brian |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210608/https://globalnews.ca/news/5899144/reality-check-scheer-immigration-refugee-queue-jumping/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Scotti |first1=Monique |title=Reality check: Are asylum seekers 'queue jumping' and other key questions |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/3278168/reality-check-are-asylum-seekers-queue-jumping-and-other-key-questions/ |access-date=9 August 2021 |work=[[Global News]] |date=March 2, 2017 |archive-date=13 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713070541/https://globalnews.ca/news/3278168/reality-check-are-asylum-seekers-queue-jumping-and-other-key-questions/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 17, 2019, Brock Harrison, Scheer's director of communication, and the CPC tweeted that the RCMP had confirmed Trudeau was under investigation for SNC-Lavalin. Scheer himself also repeated the allegation. Both tweets were removed after journalists deemed it to be false.<ref name="Zimonjic-2019">{{Cite news |last=Zimonjic |first=Peter |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Conservatives forced to delete tweet alleging Trudeau under RCMP investigation |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/tories-delete-rcmp-tweet-1.5287471?cmp=rss |access-date=September 18, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210602/https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/tories-delete-rcmp-tweet-1.5287471?cmp=rss |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Russell-2019">{{Cite web |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Reality check: No, the RCMP did not confirm an investigation into SNC-Lavalin scandal – National |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/5915114/reality-check-rcmp-did-not-confirm-snc-lavalin-scandal-investigation/ |access-date=September 18, 2019 |website=[[Global News]] |last1=Russell |first1=Andrew |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210622/https://globalnews.ca/wp-content/themes/shaw-globalnews/assets/dist/css/critical-tablet-landscape.css?m=1625604668g |url-status=live }}</ref>

A claim was circulating online that [[Bill Morneau]] was related to RCMP Commissioner [[Brenda Lucki]] through her husband, which is what was stopping the RCMP investigation regarding SNC-Lavalin. The claim is false; Lucki's husband is not related to Morneau.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bogart |first=Nicole |date=September 18, 2019 |title=Truth Tracker: No, RCMP Commissioner Brenda Lucki isn't related to Bill Morneau |url=https://election.ctvnews.ca/truth-tracker-no-rcmp-commissioner-brenda-lucki-isn-t-related-to-bill-morneau-1.4599371 |access-date=September 24, 2019 |website=Federal Election 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210637/https://election.ctvnews.ca/truth-tracker-no-rcmp-commissioner-brenda-lucki-isn-t-related-to-bill-morneau-1.4599371 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bellemare |first=Andrea |date=September 18, 2019 |title=False online rumour claims RCMP chief is married to Bill Morneau's cousin |publisher=[[CBC News]] |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/lucki-morneau-married-cousin-rumour-false-1.5288672# |access-date=September 24, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210605/https://www.cbc.ca/news/science/lucki-morneau-married-cousin-rumour-false-1.5288672 |url-status=live }}</ref> Furthermore, there has been no confirmation that there is an RCMP investigation.<ref name="Zimonjic-2019" /><ref name="Russell-2019" />

The ''[[Buffalo Chronicle]]'', an American [[fake news website]], promoted a false rumour about a sex scandal that supposedly resulted in Justin Trudeau's departure from West Point Grey Academy.<ref>{{cite web|title= Did Justin Trudeau Stop Teaching at a Vancouver Private School Under the Cloud of a Sex Scandal?|author= Dan MacGuill|date= October 9, 2019|website= [[Snopes.com]]|url= https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/trudeau-sex-scandal-school/|access-date= October 29, 2022|archive-date= October 28, 2022|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20221028232031/https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/trudeau-sex-scandal-school/|url-status= live}}</ref><ref name="NDAFactCheck">{{Cite web |last=Khandelwal |first=Devika |date=January 20, 2022 |title=False: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau had sexual relations with a minor and had her sign a two and a quarter million dollar non-disclosure agreement so no one would find out about it. |url=https://www.logicallyfacts.com/en/fact-check/false-canadian-prime-minister-justin-trudeau-had-sexual-relations-with-a-minor-and-had-her-sign-a-two-and-a-quarter-million-dollar-non-disclosure-agreement-so-no-one-would-find-out-about-it |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240204032228/https://www.logicallyfacts.com/en/fact-check/false-canadian-prime-minister-justin-trudeau-had-sexual-relations-with-a-minor-and-had-her-sign-a-two-and-a-quarter-million-dollar-non-disclosure-agreement-so-no-one-would-find-out-about-it |archive-date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=2023-02-18 |website=[[Logically (company)|Logically]] |language=en-gb}}</ref> The rumour was propagated by other fake news websites, [[gossip magazine]]s, [[Warren Kinsella]] and [[Ezra Levant]]. On October 7, 2019, the Conservatives issued a press release referencing the rumour and asking "why did Justin Trudeau leave West Point Grey Academy?". The ''Toronto Star'' and ''The Globe and Mail'' devoted multiple reporters to the story and found nothing to corroborate it. The former headmaster also released a statement that said "there is no truth to any speculation that [Trudeau] was dismissed".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anatomy of a manufactured election scandal |url=https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/10/09/anatomy-of-a-manufactured-election-scandal.html |access-date=October 10, 2019 |website=Toronto Star |last1=Chown Oved |first1=Marco |date=October 9, 2019 |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210638/https://www.thestar.com/politics/federal/2019/10/09/anatomy-of-a-manufactured-election-scandal.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McIntosh |first=Emma |date=October 10, 2019 |title=A fake Justin Trudeau sex scandal went viral. Canada's election-integrity law can't stop it |url=https://www.nationalobserver.com/2019/10/10/news/fake-justin-trudeau-sex-scandal-went-viral-canadas-election-integrity-law-cant-stop |access-date=October 10, 2019 |website=National Observer |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210641/https://www.nationalobserver.com/2019/10/10/news/fake-justin-trudeau-sex-scandal-went-viral-canadas-election-integrity-law-cant-stop |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the campaign, the NDP claimed Bill Morneau had used tax-havens when he was the executive chair of [[Morneau Shepell]], which was proven false. A probe by ''Canadians for Tax Fairness'' found that Morneau Shepell's subsidiary in the Bahamas was a legitimate business and not a way to avoid taxes.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=McIntosh |first1=Emma |last2=Syed |first2=Fatima |last3=Watson |first3=H. G. |date=October 7, 2019 |title=Six fact checks from the first official English-language leaders debate |url=https://www.nationalobserver.com/2019/10/07/news/six-fact-checks-first-official-english-language-leaders-debate |access-date=November 15, 2019 |website=National Observer |archive-date=July 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706210627/https://www.nationalobserver.com/2019/10/07/news/six-fact-checks-first-official-english-language-leaders-debate |url-status=live }}</ref> The NDP retracted the statement a few weeks after the campaign had ended.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=November 15, 2019 |title=Official NDP Statement re: Morneau Shepell |url=https://www.ndp.ca/news/official-ndp-statement-re-morneau-shepell |access-date=November 15, 2015 |website=Canada's NDP |archive-date=November 15, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191115190005/https://www.ndp.ca/news/official-ndp-statement-re-morneau-shepell |url-status=dead }}</ref>
